News.title: Migrant rapist avoids deportation from UK because he’s ‘learned his lesson’ despite taking 9 years to admit sick crime
News.content:
MIGRANT FURY Migrant rapist avoids deportation from UK because he’s ‘learned his lesson’ despite taking 9 years to admit sick crime

A RAPIST who attacked a woman while she was sleeping cannot be deported from the UK because he has “learned his lesson”.

Italian national Hendrix Ekwen, 34, has won a battle against being kicked out the country despite a report finding that he poses “a high risk of serious harm” to women.



He was sentenced to eight years in prison in May 2021 for a rape committed in 2017.

During the terrifying attack his victim “was awoken, by someone having sexual intercourse with her, whilst lying behind her.”



Ekwen, who moved to the UK in 2009, maintained his innocence at his trial at Newcastle Crown Court and sought to challenge his conviction after he was sentenced.

The Home Office sought to strip him of his European Union Settlement Scheme status and deport him to Italy.

But during a recent hearing for his appeal against his deportation, Judge Rebecca Anne Pickering accepted that he has recently made a “full acceptance of responsibility” and matured – and so allowed him to stay.

Her conclusions are despite a risk assessment carried out while he was in prison which found he displayed “sexual entitlement” and a “lack of victim empathy”.

Shockingly, the judge also took into account the fact that Ekwen went to college to study sports coaching and played football before he carried out the offence while deciding if he could stay.

Having arrived in the UK aged 18 in 2009, between 2012 and 2014, he was involved in five domestic abuse incidents and in 2015 he received a conditional discharge for possession of cannabis.



In 2020 he made an application under the European Union Settlement Scheme which would let him stay in the country.

It was later that year that he was found guilty of rape and was sentenced in 2021.

Despite the previous convictions he can now remain in the UK after Ekwen said he has “learned his lesson” and that he didn’t want to be known as “that kind of person’”.

In a judgment published on Monday [AUG 17], Judge Pickering said that the Home Office had not “established that there genuine, present and sufficiently serious threat” to public safety by allowing Ekwen to stay in the UK.

She said: “I accept that he now acknowledges that what occurred was rape. I accept that he understands the impact of his conduct upon the victim. I accept that he takes responsibility for his actions and that this development has been gradual rather than opportunistic.”



She concludes that his appeal against his deportation is allowed under the Immigration (European Economic Area) Regulations 2016 and “on human rights grounds” A Home Office spokesperson said: “We have sought permission to appeal to the Court of Appeal via the Upper Tribunal.

“Nearly 10,000 foreign criminals including murderers and rapists have been removed since the last election – a 36% increase on the 21 months prior.

“Any foreign national who receives a prison sentence in the UK is referred for deportation at the earliest opportunity and will be barred from ever returning.”

News.title: Tragedy as body found in woods during search for missing teenager
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

TRAGIC FIND Tragedy as body found in woods during search for missing teenager

A BODY has been found in a forest amid the hunt for a missing 17-year-old.

Emergency services launched a frantic search operation when Taryn Ellis-Allen was reported missing from Kessingland, Suffolk on Monday.

Taryn was last seen on Field Lane with Suffolk Lowland Search and Rescue and police launching an urgent manhunt to locate him.

Tragically, police have now confirmed that their search uncovered a body in woodland near Francis Road yesterday afternoon.





Formal identification has not yet taken place, but Taryn’s family have been informed of the sad discovery.

Police said the death is not being treated as suspicious.

A file will be prepared for the coroner.

Suffolk Constabulary said: “The body of a teenage boy has been found in Kessingland following searches for a missing 17-year-old boy.

“Taryn Ellis-Allen was last seen on Field Lane at 3:30pm on Monday, 17 August.

“Teams from the police and Suffolk Lowland Search and Rescue (SulSAR) were conducting searches in the village yesterday late afternoon, Tuesday 18 August, when they discovered a body in woodland off Francis Road.

“No formal identification has taken place, but Taryn’s family have been informed.

“The death is not being treated as suspicious, and a file will be prepared for the Coroner in due course.”

News.title: Warning as woman finds huge BAT floating in her toilet during heatwave
News.content:
BAT PAN Warning as woman finds huge BAT floating in her toilet during heatwave

BRITS have been warned to be on the lookout after a woman discovered a large bat floating in her toilet during the recent heatwave.

The creature, later nicknamed Louis, was discovered floating in the loo having flown in through an open window.



It was searching for water during the heatwave, according to experts.

Weakened and dehydrated it was carefully rescued from the bathroom in Sussex using a garden trowel before being dried off.



Sussex Wildlife Trust’s Bluesky channel pointed the finder towards expert advice and she called Sussex Bat Group volunteers.

The woman, who didn’t wish to be named, said: “I’ve learnt so much about bats from this wonderful and unsought encounter with a beautiful wild creature, including that so many are dehydrated and that the biggest single cause of injury is cats, who lurk outside their roosting places.

“And that they can find refuge in the tiniest gaps under hung tiles and in other nooks and crannies on older buildings.”

Louis was taken into the care of Sussex Bat Hospital’s Amanda Millar, who confirmed he was a Serotine – one of the UK’s larger bat species.



Though thin and exhausted on arrival, a week of rest and a steady diet of mealworms restored him to full health and ready for a test flight, proving he was fit to return home.

At dusk, Louis was driven back to the garden where he was found and released.

He flew off over the honeysuckle and into the night, with a bat later spotted flitting across the darkening sky, possibly Louis finding his way home.

Sussex Wildlife Trust is reminding residents that summer heatwaves can leave bats dehydrated and searching for water in unexpected places.

Anyone who finds a bat in distress is encouraged to contact their local Bat Group for advice.

News.title: Woman, 48, dies after fire with eight others rushed to hospital as cops launch murder probe
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BLAZE HORROR Woman, 48, dies after fire with eight others rushed to hospital as cops launch murder probe

A WOMAN has died and either others injured in a house fire, as cops launch a murder investigation.

Police were called to an address on Berkley Avenue, Hounslow, West London, just after 1am on August 19.

Officers attended the scene alongside the London Fire Brigade and London Ambulance Service before.



Nine people were taken to hospital as a result of their injuries.



Despite best efforts of medical staff, a 48-year-old woman sadly died in hospital.

Her next-of-kin have been informed and are being supported by specially trained officers.

Another woman, aged 40, remains in hospital in a life-threatening condition.



The remaining seven people – six men and one woman – have since been discharged after receiving treatment for minor injuries.

A murder investigation has since been launched.

No arrests have been made so far.

Detective Chief Inspector Neil John, who is leading the investigation, said:



“Our thoughts are first and foremost with the victim’s family and loved ones at this extremely difficult time, as well as everyone who has been injured.

“Our enquiries are progressing at pace as we work to establish the full circumstances surrounding the fire, which we believe may have been started deliberately.

“We understand this to be an isolated incident within a residential address; however, we understand it will cause concern within the local community.

“Officers will remain in the area throughout the day, and we will provide updates as our investigation continues.

“I would ask anyone with information that could assist our enquiries, including CCTV, doorbell camera or dashcam footage, to contact us.”



Anyone with information, or footage that may assist the investigation, is urged to contact police on 101, quoting CAD 359/19Aug.

Alternatively, information can be provided anonymously via the independent charity Crimestoppers on 0800 555 111 or online at crimestoppers-uk.org.

News.title: Mad Cow Disease confirmed on UK farm after 1990s outbreak led to culling of millions of cattle
News.content:
Add us as a preferred source

BOVINE FEAR Mad Cow Disease confirmed on UK farm after 1990s outbreak led to culling of millions of cattle

A CASE of Mad Cow Disease case has been confirmed on a UK farm, officials say.

The deadly disease – known as Bovine spongiform encephalopathy (BSE) – is a progressive brain sickness that can’t be treated.



The terrifying illness ravaged Britain’s cattle herds in the 1990s and led to millions of cows being slaughtered.

The latest case was confirmed in Dumfries and Galloway.



The Scottish government said precautionary measures are in place on the cow’s offspring and its cohort.

People can get infected by the human form of the illness, called Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease, by eating the meat of a contaminated animal.

Dumfries and Galloway is known for its cattle – with the region home to its own distinct breed the Belted Galloway, or “beltie”.

Food Standards Scotland said the infected animal has not entered the human food chain and there is no wider risk.

Local authorities are investigating the case, which was found due during regular BSE surveillance.

Mad Cow Disease once wreaked havoc across Britain in the 1990s as it tore through farms and even caused people to become infected.



Over 184,000 cows in the UK died from BSE and over 4.4 million cattle were slaughtered to stop the disease from spreading.

It also caused cases of the fatal variant Creutzfeldt-Jakob disease (vCJD) in humans.

Another case of Mad Cow Disease was reported on a farm in Essex last year.

And a separate case was reported in Somerset in September 2021.

Prior to that, a case of BSE was reported at a farm in Aberdeenshire in October 2018 – the first case of the disease in three years in the UK and the first confirmed in Scotland since 2008.



Previously, a dead cow with the disease was discovered in Wales in 2015.

PARK HORROR Boy, 12, charged after eight-year-old girl ‘sexually assaulted at UK playpark’

A 12-YEAR-OLD boy has been charged with sexual assault after an 8-year-old girl was reportedly attacked at a playpark.

Police were alerted to the alleged assault in Macduff, Aberdeenshire, Scotland, on Monday, August 10.

An investigation into the alleged sexual assault was launched and a 12-year-old boy was charged in connection.

A report will be provided to the procurator fiscal.

“Officers are following a positive line of enquiry.”

News.title: Child ‘heard counting down 3, 2, 1’ before boy, 5, fell to death from ‘faulty’ 15th floor window
News.content:
PLUNGE TRAGEDY Child ‘heard counting down 3, 2, 1’ before boy, 5, fell to death from ‘faulty’ 15th floor window

A CHILD was heard counting down before a 5-year-old boy fell to his death from an allegedly faulty 15th floor window.

Aalim Ahmed was killed instantly when he landed on railings at the bottom of a block of flats in Plaistow, East London, shortly before 6am on May 16, 2024.



An inquest into the tragedy has since heard that grainy audio, from CCTV outside of the block of flats, picked up a child counting down in the moments before Aalim’s death.

A young child’s voice is twice heard counting down “3, 2, 1” and “a loud clang” follows some seconds later, Walthamstow Coroners’ Court was told.



Detective Constable Joe Linton carried out a review of CCTV footage outside Jacobs House.

He said that in footage from the building, “you can hear another young child shouting ‘Aalim’”, who would appear to be the boy’s brother who was then three years old.



In the footage played to the court Aalim’s dad, who discovered him after the fall, was “topless and clearly distressed.”

DC Linton said “it is most likely from the footage available” that Aalim had “jumped out” of the flat “of his own accord without the presence of a third party.”



A post-mortem found Aalim died from “multiple injuries due to or as a consequence of trauma” from a “fall from height.”

Detective Inspector Jamie Humm, who investigated the incident, said there was “no evidence or suspicion he [Aalim] had been forced.”

He noted that: “The flat was well furnished and it was clearly a loving environment for a child.”

Humm told how soon after arriving at the scene he was satisfied “there was no evidence of a crime not that I thought there would be.”

Aalim’s dad, Makail Ahmed, and his mum, Sahra Osman, described their son’s sad death as “preventable” and blamed Newham Council.



Sahra told the court she was “scared” and “horrified” when the local authority put them in the top-floor flat, which needed repairs.

She had lodged several complaints about the safety of the flat, she claims.

Sahra said she had called the council to complain and begged them to help.

She told the inquest “the window was wide open, it would not lock, it was hanging.”

Sahra stressed it was a safety issue for her children, but said the council did not treat it as “an emergency.”



Despite repairs being carried out and engineers having been to look at the work, Sahra said she felt the flat was still not safe and there were “open windows.”

All the windows were closed before the family went to bed, the inquest heard.

It is still not known how the child would have got to the window, the court heard.

Assistant coroner Ian Wade, who described the audio recording as “poignant”, said: “Aalim at his tender age and with his autism could not have known what could have happened.

“It seems to me that he would not have meant to have deliberately taken the stance to have harmed himself.”



Robert O’Sullivan, of the London Ambulance Service, recalled that “a number of colleagues were visibly shocked” after finding the boy.

In his statement, he recalled: “There was an adult male shouting ‘I have told them about the window’.”

The right-hand kitchen window was open when emergency crews arrived on the tragic scene.

Sergeant Christopher Diment, who was among the officers who attended the scene, said Aalim’s dad was “clearly distraught, pacing around and shouting”, and was “overcome with grief.”

When they went into the flat Makail was saying something about the state of the windows, he told the court.



Sahra denied any allegation that she may have “forced” the window open to cope in hot weather.

Aalim’s family had worked with an occupational therapist to help support his needs.

His teacher Esme Johns said the boy had to be reminded not to do or touch something because he “lacked danger awareness.”

She added: “He would say sorry, but found it difficult to understand.”

The hearing continues.

News.title: Tupac murder trial hit by ‘snitches get stitches’ snag as ‘hostile’ witness confronts lawyers in courtroom outburst
News.content:
A HOSTILE witness clashed with attorneys during the murder trial of a Compton gang shot caller accused of plotting the drive-by shooting of rapper Tupac Shakur.

James McDonald, a former Mob Piru Bloods gangbanger, admitted to being reluctant to testify against Duane “Keefe D” Davis at his murder trial despite his mutual dislike for each other.



When asked by prosecutor Binu Palal if he was voluntarily taking the stand, McDonald sharply responded, “Not at all,” adding that he was subpoenaed by the court.

McDonald, who goes by Mob James, dared the prosecutor to treat him as a hostile witness and was hesitant to provide details about the deadly rivalry between the Piru Bloods and the South Side Compton Crips in the 1990s.



“I’m aware of a lot of things, things that was going on. People ain’t talked about it in 30 years – today ain’t one of them,” he told prosecutors after being asked if he knew why Shakur and his entourage attacked Orlando Anderson at the MGM Grand Casino Hotel in Las Vegas on September 7, 1996.

“I told every attorney that tried to get me to come here, you better treat me as a hostile witness, and I think that’s why I’m about to go down because you’re asking me questions – I can’t answer those questions.



“People put themselves in situations, like myself, I’m guilty as everybody else, I put myself in situations to protect something and somebody that didn’t have nothing to do with me.

“I did it for a paycheck. I did it on some just because. I’m older now, I get it, but we did things for all the wrong reasons at that time, in them days.”

McDonald, who was a lieutenant for Death Row Records co-founder Marion “Suge” Knight, became more irritated during cross-examination when he was asked by Davis’ defense attorney to describe the tension in Compton after Shakur’s shooting.

“You sure you want me to answer that?” McDonald asked Michael Sanft, Davis’ attorney.



“I have ways of wording it but you asking me a question and like I explained to [the prosecution] I don’t want to send [Davis] to prison,” he added pointing at Davis.

“Even though we don’t like each other. I don’t want to send him to prison. That’s why I’m here acting the way I am. You asking me questions that could hurt him.”

When Sanft continued to ask about his knowledge of the individuals that were present at the scene where Shakur was shot, McDonald scoffed at the question and put his head on the desk.

“Talk to your lawyer, man. This dude is tripping,” he told Davis.

“I’m not going to explain that. I can’t answer that.”



McDonald, who was on the stand for nearly 40 minutes, continued his combative attitude, saying the only reason he’s testifying is because he was threatened with being held in contempt of court if he didn’t show up.



“Like I explained to everybody in here, you ask me something I’m going to be honest about it,” he said.

“You ask me something I don’t want to talk about we gone have a problem. Treat me as a hostile witness.

“You’re not going to talk to me and tell me as a grown man what I have to do up here.

“I’m not finna send him to prison. You are,” McDonald said pointing at Sanft, who responded, “So the accusation now is because we’re trying to ask you questions you’re blaming it on me.”

McDonald clapped back, saying, “You’re asking me questions. If I answer your questions, we’re going to have a problem in here, a misunderstanding.



“You’re asking me something that wouldn’t be good for [Davis].”

Before stepping off the stand, McDonald apologized to the court and delivered a final message to Davis, saying, “What you’re going through, brother, is what you’re going through.

“I didn’t want to be a part of that and I’m not a part of that,” he told Davis, who remained stoic.

As Davis’ trial enters its third day, retired Los Angeles Police Detective Moses Castillo said the gang mantra of “snitches get stitches” continues to hang over the case.

“When you’re in this circle of gangs and gang involvement, you don’t want to be a snitch,” Castillo told Fox News.



“You don’t wanna be that person that’s being classified as a rat because as they say, snitches get stitches, and that is really true.”

Castillo said he believes the prosecution is going to have to call the co-author of Davis’ memoir, Compton Street Legend, to strengthen their case.

RECOMMENDED STORIES

“I suspect the prosecution is going to have to have to call the writer of this book and ask him point-blank and directly: Did you write this based on what Davis told you,” Castillo, referring to Yusef Jah.

“And then if he says yes, and this is what he told me, then it’s gonna be very hard to dispute that fact.”

News.title: Tourist thought 'you're gone' as he fell down 30ft sinkhole that left his BMW teetering above him
News.content:
Tourist thought 'you're gone' as he fell down 30ft sinkhole that left his BMW teetering above him

Ex-miner Ian Haynes was preparing to conclude his two-week campervan holiday in Cornwall when he fell down a gaping sinkhole that had opened below his BMW

View 5 Images An ex-miner was left with PTSD after falling 30 feet (Image: Ian Haynes)

A former miner who plunged 30 feet down a massive sinkhole after it unexpectedly appeared under his BMW thought his "time was over" when the ground opened up beneath him.

‌



Ian Haynes, 62, was enjoying a holiday in the Higher Trevaskis Caravan and Camping Park, in Connor Downs, Cornwall, in July when the gaping hole opened up below his parked car. He plunged what he believed was four stories before landing in a pool of water, while his car teetered at the opening above him.

‌



The former miner, who is from Nottinghamshire, thought he was "gone" as he landed in the murky depths below the campsite car park, and waited nearly an hour for a 60-strong emergency team to pluck him out.

‌



View 5 Images The sinkhole was initially much smaller, and only encompassed the former miner's BMW rear wheel (Image: Ian Haynes)

The pothole-sized opening under Ian's car unexpectedly swallowed the granddad after rapidly growing inside from under the wheel of his BMW. Within the space of a day it had expanded to the size of a vehicle. During the fall, Ian said he had just enough time to consider himself a goner before he hit the water below.

He told CornwallLive: "I thought, 'you're gone, mate, your time is over'. I was near the door [of the car] and I just went through the concrete.

‌



"You can imagine, I'm going down a hole, looking up and seeing a car wheel above my head and this hole is getting smaller and smaller. My grandchildren were playing in that spot while we were on holiday and the caravan next door to us was two retired old ladies who had to walk past that spot to go to the toilet every day."

View 5 Images A team of 60 people rescued the miner following his fall (Image: Ian Haynes)

Ian said that, while he is physically recovered from the incident, he is "still suffering" with wobbles caused by the shock of the fall. He added: "I'm still suffering and at 4am I'm jumping out of bed and feeling like I'm falling down the hole again."

‌



He was sent tumbling down the hole the day before he was due to leave his campsite, and after calling the site owner to investigate the still modestly sized opening when he noticed the front of his car had "dropped down".

He spent 55 minutes clinging to the walls of the sinkhole fearing that any moment could be his last as he desperately awaited the arrival of emergency services. He was eventually pulled to the service by dozens of fire service workers who lowered a rope and safety harness down to him.

View 5 Images The miner felt he was 'gone' as he fell (Image: Ian Haynes)

‌



Recounting the rescue, he said: "I knew what to do, Their job was easy. They threw me a rope down and, like a plastic nappy on a safety harness, I knew how to fasten it and they winched me back up. "

While he exited the hole with a few cuts and scrapes, the emotional toll has remained in the form of post traumatic stress disorder (PTSD). He praised the way the ordeal was handled, saying staff were "incredibly caring and concerned" for him.

Devon and Cornwall Police said: "Officers attended Gwinear Road shortly after 6pm on 24 July to provide support to emergency services who were responding to a report of a man having fallen into a sinkhole. A number of people were cleared from the area for safety."

‌



View 5 Images Ian escaped with a few cuts and scrapes, but was left with a mental toll (Image: Ian Haynes)

A spokesperson for Cornwall Fire and Rescue Service said: "Cornwall Fire and Rescue Service was called to Connor Downs, Hayle, on July 24 at around 6pm.

"Firefighters used line rescue equipment to rescue a casualty who was approximately 30ft down a sinkhole. The casualty was left in the care of the ambulance service." A spokesperson for Higher Trevaskis Caravan and Camping Park said: "We would like to thank everyone involved in the rescue and also the experts involved in making the site safe for our customers which is always our number one priority.

Article continues below

"An unrecorded, historical mining feature opened up in an isolated area of the park. Our emergency safety protocols were activated instantly, and the emergency services were called which lead to the rescue of a guest.

"The said guest was taken to hospital with cuts and bruises and given the all clear by the hospital, returning here soon after. Specialist engineers are already managing the permanent capping process."

News.title: EasyJet cancels all flights from UK airport - full list of destinations scrapped
News.content:
EasyJet cancels all flights from UK airport - full list of destinations scrapped

EasyJet has confirmed flights from Leeds Bradford Airport (LBA) will cease from January 2027 as the airline focuses on 'maintaining and developing' its 'most popular' routes

View 2 Images EasyJet says it will be focusing on its 'most popular' routes (Image: Jam Press)

EasyJet has announced it will no longer be running flights from Leeds Bradford Airport (LBA).

‌



The budget airline said it was withdrawing from the airport next January to "focus on maintaining and developing" its "most popular" routes.

‌



Passengers travelling from LBA were able to fly to Barcelona, Paris, Belfast, Malaga, Mallorca and Geneva - but these journeys will cease from January 5, 2027.

‌



Anyone with EasyJet bookings beyond that date have been offered a free transfer to flights from an alternative airport or a refund, the airline said.

EasyJet has not yet confirmed whether all scheduled flights to its destinations from Leeds Bradford Airport will go ahead.

View 2 Images Leeds Bradford Airport offered EasyJet flights to Barcelona, Paris, Belfast, Malaga, Mallorca and Geneva (Image: SWNS)

‌



But its website showed no available flights from Leeds Bradford to Geneva. Flights to Malaga and Mallorca meanwhile appeared to stop running after November.

Flights to Barcelona, Paris and Belfast still appeared to be available until January.

An EasyJet spokesperson said: "Following a review of our routes from Leeds Bradford Airport, we have made the decision to no longer operate flights from the airport after 5 January.

‌



"Our focus is on maintaining and developing routes which prove most popular with customers."

"We have contacted customers with bookings beyond this date to provide them with advance notice and inform them of their options, including a free transfer to flights from an alternative airport or a refund, and we are very sorry for the inconvenience caused.

"We value the relationship we have built with Leeds Bradford Airport and we always keep options for our network under review, with the aim of providing more choice and connectivity where we see demand."

Article continues below

EasyJet began flights from Leeds Bradford Airport in 2010.

News.title: Should the state pension triple lock be scrapped? Take our poll and have your say
News.content:
Should the state pension triple lock be scrapped? Take our poll and have your say

The triple lock guarantees the state pension rises every April whichever is higher out of inflation, wages or 2.5% - but should it be kept or scrapped?

View Image Should the triple lock be axed? (Image: Getty Images/Connect Images)

The state pension is likely to rise by more than £500 a year from next April under the triple lock promise.

‌



The triple lock guarantees the state pension rises every April whichever is higher out of inflation (using the previous September inflation figure), wages (average growth between May and July) or 2.5%.

‌



But we're asking Mirror readers for their thoughts on whether the triple lock should be kept in place, or whether it should be scrapped. Have your say below.

‌



Wage growth is likely to be the figure used to determine the state pension increase for April 2027. Latest figures from the Office for National Statistics (ONS) shows average growth, including bonuses, fell to 4.1% in the three months to June.

In comparison, inflation is now at 2.9%. This means unless inflation rises sharply in the next three months, it is the wage growth which will be the higher figure.

‌



If earnings growth next month is unchanged, an increase of 4.1% would add a little over £500 a year to the state pension. The full new state pension is currently worth £241.30 a week and this increase would take it to £251.20.

Wage growth was also used to determine the state pension increase for this April, with state pension payments rising by 4.8% earlier this year.

But the state pension is also set to rise above the tax-free allowance, which is the amount you can earn every tax year before you start to pay tax, from next year.

‌



The full new state pension is currently worth £12,547.60 a year, while the personal allowance is £12,570. The Treasury has pledged that income tax will not be charged on people who only receive the state pension.

You get the new state pension if you're a man born on or after April 6, 1951, or if you're a woman born on or after April 6, 1953. Someone on a full basic state pension would see their weekly amount rise from £184.90 per week to around £192.50 from next April.

These are the full amounts of state pension that you can get. You may receive less than these amounts depending on your National Insurance record.

Article continues below

The state pension age is currently set at 66 for men and women but is now gradually increasing to age 67. There are already plans in place for the state pension age to rise again to 68 between April 2044 and April 2046 but reports suggest this could be brought forward. The Government has not yet officially announced any changes to this timetable.

News.title: 'I spoke to serial killer Robert Maudsley - he acknowledged chilling similarity'
News.content:
There is a click on the line then an announcement that the call is being monitored by HM Prison Service.

The line is suddenly cut off by an alert from the Government about the danger of forest fires.

Then the quiet, calm voice of Robert Maudsley, the quadruple killer nicknamed 'Hannibal the Cannibal,' is heard again.

He proceeds to describe his last 52 years behind bars - the longest stretch served by any UK prisoner - and his extraordinary world record for solitary confinement.

‌



It is a lifetime alone in a cell; 17,500 consecutive days after he attacked and killed three fellow inmates, the first in Broadmoor almost half a century ago, in 1977, then another two on the same day in 1978.

There is no bitterness about the time lost.

But there is also no regret about what he did all those years ago, when he first left home after years of sadistic abuse at the hands of his own father, just a desire to calmly explain his crimes.

In the era of early release for prisoners, Maudsley says he believes he should die behind bars, stating that this is justice for the crimes he committed.

‌



View 2 Images Robert Maudsley spoke of his life in a prison cell for the past 52 years (Image: Unknown)

But he cannot help thinking of a possible taste of freedom: his desire to experience the four seasons once more and feel the sun on his face, and the simple joy of the wind blowing through his open cell window.

He admits that people are fascinated with him because they think Hannibal Lecter in the hit movie 'The Silence of the Lambs' was based on his life story.

He says: "It insinuates that connection to me, and I think Hannibal Lecter and the actual film have more appeal than I will ever have.

‌



"There is a similarity to Anthony Hopkins' character in terms of his desire to understand people and serial killer Buffalo Bill.

View 2 Images Dr Bob Johnson met Maudsley and had therapy sessions with him in the 1980s (Image: YouTube/@shaunattwoodOFFICIAL)

"I have a fascination with learning about myself and other people and that would help me come to terms with what happened to me."

He believes that if he had been left in the care of Dr Bob Johnson, his prison psychiatrist for a brief spell in the 1980s, that he would no longer be a danger to society.

‌



And Dr Johnson agrees.

He has not had a visit from his brothers on Merseyside since February, 2025, nor from his long time partner Loveinia MacKenney.

He believes that the refusal to allow him to see his family and friends is a further attempt to 'break him', to deny him any human contact.

His voice reflects his Merseyside roots, the Liverpool accent is still strong.

‌



Robert Maudsley patiently explains that he knows that he will die in a prison cell and that he will never experience the outside world, the seasons, the sunshine on his face, or the simple human pleasures that he craves.

He acknowledges that is the punishment which he deserves, which is a rare thing indeed these days.

News.title: Hayden Panettiere dies aged 36: Unexpected death triggers criminal investigation
News.content:
Hayden Panettiere has died at the age of 36, with the initial investigation from police finding there was 'no foul play' and autopsy results confirming 'no signs of trauma'

US actress Hayden Panettiere, who was best known for her roles in Heroes and Nashville, has died aged 36. Her death was confirmed by her representatives and followed by a statement.

The statement from her father, Skip, read: “It is with profound sadness that we share the tragic passing of our beloved Hayden. She was an incredible light and a force of nature who brought immeasurable love and joy to all who knew her — and to the millions who watched her onscreen.”

Meanwhile, her mother spoke the first time on Tuesday, firing shots at ex Brian Hickerson. She said: "I think Hayden was an amazingly talented person in so many departments and I think young people who grow up in the entertainment industry -- it is a struggle and it's a very challenging industry and it's not unusual for them to sadly find the wrong path."

She also added: "This person in her life that we have been trying to get rid of for quite some time was with her at her death, and that was Brian Hickerson."

The Coroner's office confirmed that Hayden's autopsy showed 'no signs of trauma' at the time of her death. It had been reported that the police were responding to a call about a suspected "cardiac arrest". A police report later revealed that both her ex Hickerson and his brother Zach were at the scene at the time of her death.

911 audio footage also heard dispatchers discuss a suspected overdose. Both Narcan and Epinephrine were reportedly brought to the scene by emergency services Panettiere's cause of death has not been announced at this time.

A preliminary police investigation has confirmed there were no signs of "foul play or suspicious circumstances" when they arrived at her home after a 911 emergency call from an acquaintance of Panettiere's.

News.title: Monzo down - recap: Banking app users 'can't transfer money' as thousands report problems
News.content:
Thousands of Monzo customers were hit by problems with the app and bank transfers before the outage was resolved.

Thousands of Monzo customers were hit by app and bank transfer problems during an outage on Wednesday afternoon.

Downdetector recorded a peak of 3,246 reports, as customers complained about problems accessing parts of the app and moving money.

Monzo activated Monzo Stand-in, its fully independent backup bank, while it investigated what it described as a technical issue. The bank said card payments, cash withdrawals and bank transfers remained available through the backup service.

A Monzo spokesperson later confirmed the issue had been resolved, saying: “For a short period today, we activated Monzo Stand-in, our fully independent backup bank while we investigated an issue affecting customers. This technical issue has been resolved, and all of our services are now back up and running. We're sorry for any inconvenience and thank customers for their patience.”

News.title: UK's longest-serving prisoner Robert Maudsley: I want to stay behind bars – I could kill again
News.content:
UK's longest-serving prisoner Robert Maudsley: I want to stay behind bars – I could kill again

EXCLUSIVE: In his first interview in almost 50 years, quadruple killer Robert Maudsley, 73, spoke to the Mirror from his prison cell on E Wing in HMP Whitemoor, Cambridgeshire

Britain's longest serving inmate Robert Maudsley 'Hannibal the Cannibal' talks about being in prison for 52 years

Britain's longest serving prisoner has told of his 17,500 consecutive days in solitary confinement - and warns that he could kill again.

‌



In his first interview in 50 years, quadruple killer Robert Maudsley, 73, spoke to the Mirror from 'E' Wing of HMP Whitemoor, Cambridgeshire.

‌



Maudsley was nicknamed 'Hannibal the Cannibal' after he killed a fellow inmate and was said to have eaten his brain with a spoon. A post-mortem proved that claim untrue.

‌



The shocking case has been likened to the fictional killer Hannibal Lecter in the 1991 hit movie 'The Silence of the Lambs,' the disturbing portrayal of a cannibalistic serial killer for which Anthony Hopkins won an Oscar.

Maudsley has spent the best part of 47 years either in segregation or solitary, setting a world record of 17,500 consecutive days alone.

He has now served 52 years behind bars, and was once described as the most dangerous prisoner in the UK penal system.

‌



After killing three fellow inmates, he was deemed such a risk that he had to stick his feet out of a gap at the bottom of his cell door to have his toenails clipped.

In a wide-ranging, hour-long interview, he spoke about his life behind bars, how he has found love for the first time with his partner Loveinia MacKenney, and why he believes that he should be locked up for life.

He told the Mirror: "I have to be honest and say that if I had the opportunity to harm a sex offender then I would do so. If I met someone who had sexually abused me, I would do my best to kill them.

‌



"When I went back to Liverpool, I had the desire to kill both my parents, and then I had the desire to harm myself. I wanted to get my own back, including on my father, and I visualised killing my parents."

View 5 Images The last time Robert Maudsley was seen by the outside world was in a documentary almost 50 years ago (Image: BBC)

Parents' nicknames

Maudsley, one of 12 children, told his prison psychologist Dr Bob Johnson, also interviewed by the Mirror, that his father abused him and locked him in a cupboard under the stairs at the family home.

‌



Known as 'Uncle Bob' to his family, Maudsley added: "We called them the drunk, and the witch. We referred to them by those names rather than as mother and father.

"I do have the possibility within myself to kill again, but with therapy, I think that I could overcome that."

Maudsley killed two people in one day

Prison barbers refused to enter Maudsley's cell in Wakefield jail after he killed two inmates there on the same day in 1977.

‌



He told a prison guard, "You'll be two down on the roll call," after walking away from his victims' bodies.

He grew his hair and beard long, and refused to co-operate with prison staff.

A Perspex wall had to be installed in his 18 ft by 15 ft wide cell so he could not throw liquids or missiles at his guards.

‌



That again led to comparisons with the cell that held the fictitious killer Hannibal Lecter.

"On the high security unit at Wakefield, when they built them, the cell door opened flush to the wall," Maudsley recalled.

"About two feet in front of the cell door, there was a barred gate with Perspex so I could not throw anything at the guards when they entered.

‌



"It was like a normal cell except down the centre of it, there was a TV shared with the cell next door.

"It had wires connected to speakers inside our cells. We had to flip the speaker, there was a diagonal screen so we could then watch the TV.

"I was not in a Perspex box but it did have the Perspex wall. For a long time I just had a mattress and a pot to pee in.

‌



"I would have to put my feet through a gap in the door for the officers to cut my toenails.

"For 12-13 months I did not shave or cut my hair, and yes, I was like the Wild Man of Borneo."

View 5 Images Robert Maudsley as a child in his native Liverpool (Image: Liverpool Echo)

‌



Charlie Bronson

He laughs but adds: "It was psychological. I thought that if you want to treat me like an animal, I will act like one.

"I am refusing all prison food at the moment. I buy whatever I can get from the prison shop in protest at the way I am being treated.

"That is about the refusal of my visits, my conditions overall."

‌



For many years at Wakefield, the notorious prisoner Charlie Bronson was his 'next door neighbour' and they shared the TV in their high-security cells.

"They (cells) were mirror images of each other. We could talk to each other through the windows," added Maudsley.

"But we did not really get on.

‌



"He was a narcissist, he always had to be top dog, trying to put me down at every opportunity to establish dominance.

"We had a falling-out over what programme to watch one night. So I asked a prison guard to open the gap for the TV and I put my foot through it.

"Charlie was not very happy about that." Maudsley says his treatment at Whitemoor has been 'sinister'.

‌



View 5 Images Robert Maudsley seen as a young man in his prison cell. He is now 73, and has spent 52 years behind bars (Image: Unknown)

"They believed the stories in the newspapers and books," he added.

"They thought I was dangerous, then their treatment became more sinister.

‌



"They put me on the punishment yard, that is the thing that gets to me.

"You cannot see anything, the walls are so high, there is no pond, it is sterile.

"I can hear the other prisoners laughing and joking with each other.

‌



"It was the prison staff who got sick of that regime. They got bored with it."

Maudsley, Prisoner A9888AA, was first sent to Broadmoor in 1974 for the manslaughter of child sex offender John Farrell.

He killed another patient, a convicted child molester, at the high-security hospital in 1976.

‌



He was then moved to Wakefield, where he murdered two of his fellow inmates, both described as child sex offenders.

He is unapologetic about the deaths of any of his victims.

View 5 Images Loveinia MacKenney has been writing to Robert Maudsley for around five years (Image: Daily Mirror)

‌



Gogglebox

When he last tasted freedom at the age of 21 in 1974, Harold Wilson had just succeeded Edward Heath as Prime Minister, a loaf of white bread cost 14p and Paper Lace were at No 1 with 'Billy, Don't Be A Hero'.

He is fighting to see Loveinia and has not had a visit since Feb. 2025. He is desperate to meet her for the first time after almost five years of correspondence and phone calls.

‌



He claims visit requests since his transfer to Whitemoor from Wakefield in April, 2025, have been refused.

"The denial of visits has added to my isolation, there is no doubt about that," he said. "I am locked in my cell for 22 and a half hours per day, getting only 75 minutes to exercise and shower.

"I always put the radio on in the morning and listen to Magic Classical. I love classical music. I watch TV.

‌



"Now I get 28 channels. My favourite show is Gogglebox, and I like The Chase with Bradley Walsh, Pointless, and Countdown.

"I watch them, to keep my mind occupied and active so I don't start to deteriorate."

'I see the whole life term as justified'

Despite early prisoner release, he insisted: "I want to spend the rest of my life behind bars to pay for what I have done.

‌



"I see the whole life term as justified for my crimes. The way I cope is that every time I wake up in the morning I think, 'It is a new day'.

"It may be like what I have experienced before, but there may be something different."

After spending almost his entire adult life in solitary confinement, he finds joy in a wisp of a breeze coming through his cell window.

‌



He would love to experience 'winter, autumn, spring, and summer again'. "To feel the wind when it blows through my window at night is fantastic," he said. "To feel the sun on your skin, it is the little things that you miss."

The last time the outside world saw him, he was in his 20s during the filming of a BBC documentary.

He says that he now looks like the late American country singer Kenny Rogers, due to his clipped white beard and hair.

‌



He loves Schubert's "Ave Maria". "It is beautiful," he says. "When you listen to that, you are no longer in the prison cell, you could be anywhere in the world.

"Mozart also did some beautiful things. A pop record can take me back to my childhood.

"For me, it is the Rolling Stones rather than the Beatles. "

‌



Given the chance to taste freedom, he would live on an island with Londoner Loveinia, 71, a mum-of-one.

With her, he has found love for the first time in his life.

"With my parents, there was no love," he says. "It has given me hope and for as long as we are alive, we will both have each other and give each other strength. The love we share keeps us going, it is the first time I have ever loved someone in the way that I love her."

‌



View 5 Images A letter from Maudsley about his treatment

Psychiatrist Bob Johnson, 89, who treated Maudsley in Parkhurst back in the 1980s, said: "I would sit alone with him in his cell and we'd discuss our favourite composer Schubert.

"It would be far better to use his intelligence and get him working, he could have earned thousands in compensation to be paid to the victims' families.

‌



"I believe that he would not have killed again with the help of our sessions. What he has had since is institutional sadism."

In the Hollywood film 'The Shawshank Redemption,' the Morgan Freeman character Ellis 'Red' Redding is asked what he would say if he could speak to his younger self, before he committed his crimes.

Maudsley was asked the same question. He replied: "It is difficult because there are so many thanks that I could say to that 20-year-old.

Article continues below

"The main thing, irrespective of what happened, is that I had the strength to get up. I know inwardly that I would have the strength to keep going."

There is no regret for his 52 years behind bars. Unlike Red in the film, he has no desire to change: "The people I killed did not see their victims as human, in a sense I was a piece of meat.

"I treated them the same, and got my revenge that way. If I say that I should not have done that, the years in prison would be worthless."

News.title: Boeing whistleblower John Barnett's mysterious death and furious final words
News.content:
Boeing whistleblower John Barnett's mysterious death and furious final words

WARNING - DISTRESSING CONTENT: New Netflix documentary Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing, investigates the story of Boeing whistleblower John Barnett, who was found dead in his truck in 2024

View 5 Images John Barnett was found dead on March 9 from a 'self-inflicted' wound

John Barnett worked for Boeing for 32 years before turning whistleblower and dying in mysterious circumstances.

‌



New Netflix documentary, Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing, explores the story of Barnett, who publicly condemned Boeing's safety processes before he was found dead in his truck. He was in the process of testifying against the company.

‌



From 2010, Barnett was employed as a quality manager at the North Charleston plant, which built the longhaul 787 Dreamliner, before retiring in 2017 on health grounds.

‌



After Boeing merged with a former rival McDonnell Douglas, several former Boeing employees alleged the company started focussing more on increasing profits rather than safety and quality.

View 5 Images John Barnett turned whistleblower having worked at Boeing for more than 30 years (Image: Courtesy of AIRFLIX-Maxwell Archives)

Barnett told the Today Show before his death: "From day one, it's just all been about schedule, and hurry up, and just get it done. Push a plane out. We're behind schedule. We don't have time to worry about issues that y'all bring up."

‌



He alleged there were severe production and safety flaws such as defective oxygen systems and metal shavings near critical wiring on the 787 Dreamliner program.

Just before he left Boeing in 2017, Barnett filed a complaint against the company, accusing bosses of retaliating against him for raising safety concerns. He was outspoken on the issue with journalists - and in 2022 appeared in acclaimed director Rory Kennedy's investigative film Downfall: The Case Against Boeing.

But then, on March 9, 2024, Barnett was found dead in his truck with a gunshot wound to his head.

‌



Deeply affected by Barnett's death and ongoing concerns about Boeing's safety culture, Kennedy reunited with her team to produce the documentary sequel, Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing, which is being released on August 19, 2026.

View 5 Images Director Rory Kennedy was deeply affected by Barnett's death (Image: Variety via Getty Images)

Speaking to the Guardian about Barnett's death, Oscar-nominated filmmaker Kennedy said: "I was horrified and heartbroken. I spoke to his mom pretty immediately after we had heard that news. She said to me, 'We need to make sure John's story gets out there,' and that was a big part of why we decided to revisit this.

‌



"I've never done a documentary follow-up in this kind of way, but we all felt that Boeing is such a big company, and we all fly these airplanes all over the world. I don't want one of these planes falling out of the sky, and I feel like I have a lot of inside knowledge and also connections to understanding what's going on inside of Boeing, and I just felt like we've got to stay at this."

Details of the circumstances surrounding Barnett's death came to light when his mother sued Boeing in a wrongful death suit in March 2025. The complaint alleged that Barnett was subjected to a campaign of harassment, abuse and humiliation after he raised concerns about safety issues. It further claimed that the conduct of the company was "the clear, foreseeable cause" of his death. In September that year, Boeing settled the lawsuit, agreeing to pay at least $50,000 to Barnett's mother, who, in return, agreed to drop her claims that the company contributed to her son's death by suicide.

The complaint contained a copy of Barnett's suicide note, and the annexes presented the full police report concluding that he died by his own hand.

‌



View 5 Images John Barnett was found dead in his truck after he failed to show up for the second part of his testimony in a bombshell lawsuit against Boeing

In conversations with Fortune in March 2025, the family's longstanding counsel Rob Turkewitz added further details on his client's last hours.

He said that on the evening of March 8, 2024, Barnett left the law offices of Boeing's outside counsel in Charleston after testifying for two days in his OSHA case against the company. OSHA rules make it unlawful to retaliate against a whistleblower.

‌



Barnett was giving his account of how Boeing allegedly violated its own policies and procedures, and FAA rules, during his seven years as a quality inspector at the North Charleston plant.

He'd delayed a trip back to his home in Louisiana to finish his deposition the next day, which was a Saturday. Videos cited in the police report show Barnett leaving the hotel around 8:30pm, and getting in his orange Dodge truck.

When Barnett failed to show up the next morning for his final round of testimony, Turkewitz called the Holiday Inn to conduct a welfare check. It was then that a hotel employee saw Barnett slumped in the front seat of his vehicle.

‌



Charleston police arrived to discover Barnett barefoot and clutching a Smith and Wesson pistol in his right hand. His right temple showed a bullet entry wound, and an exit wound appeared in the back of his head.

View 5 Images Part of the note found next to John Barnett's body

On the seat next to Barnett's body lay a message written on a single page of a red-covered notebook, with sentences written in all directions.

‌



It contained phrases including: "America come together or die!!! Pray that the motherfk…ers who destroyed my life pay!!! I pray that Boeing pays!!! Bury me face down so that Boeing and their lying ass leaders can kiss my ass."

Elsewhere: "I can't do this any longer!!! F-k Boeing!!! Family and friends, I love you'll [sic]."

"To my family and friends, I found my purpose! I am at peace! I love you more John/Mitch Barnett aka Swampy Fununcle Mitch."

Article continues below

The complaint also included a heartbreaking email that Barnett sent Turkewitz in 2021, which read: "I can understand the direct costs that we can establish, ie lost pay, bonuses, etc. What I'm struggling with is how do you restore a person’s overall outlook on life? I used to be a very happy-go-lucky guy who loved his job and the products he built. I had a very positive outlook on life. Boeing absolutely destroyed my outlook on life. What is a person's 'outlook on life' worth? How to put a price on that?'"

Freefall: A Reckoning for Boeing is scheduled to debut on Netflix on August 19, 2026 .

News.title: Couple and teenage daughter who died in water off Shoreham named by police
News.content:
Three members of the same family who died after getting into difficulty in the sea off Shoreham have been named by police.

Hassan El-Khawas, 55, and Zeina Alayn, 37, and their 14-year-old daughter Sara El-Khawas are thought to have gone into the water near Shoreham Fort on Tuesday, Sussex Police said.

A younger girl from the same family, who was pulled from the water with them, remains in hospital in a critical condition.

Police said the family had travelled from their London home to visit Shoreham and after reviewing CCTV footage investigators say they believe the deaths were a tragic accident with no third-party involvement.

The Palestinian Forum said the family were British citizens of Palestinian origin, with roots in the Rashidieh refugee camp in Lebanon. Earlier, the Palestinian embassy in London told the BBC that Hassan El-Khawas had been a refugee.

Adnan Hmidan, chairman of the Palestinian Forum in Britain, said the community was "deeply shocked and saddened" by what had happened.

He said two other children were on the shore at the time of the incident.

"Our thoughts and prayers are with the entire family, particularly the children, who are facing an unimaginable loss," he said.

The Palestinian Embassy in London said it was closely monitoring the incident and contacting British authorities to establish the circumstances and check on the condition of the girl in hospital.

A statement issued by the embassy sent condolences to the family and the UK's Palestinian community and wished the girl a speedy recovery.

News.title: Track defect found on approach to site of Lewes derailment, initial report says
News.content:
A defect was found on railway tracks in East Sussex at the site where a train derailed leaving 30 injured, a report says.

Initial findings from the Rail Accident Investigation Branch (RAIB) found an "irregularity" with the tracks near Lewes where three carriages tumbled down an embankment last Thursday.

The RAIB, which is continuing to investigate the derailment, said it had received "several reports of rough riding at the location of the derailment from passengers on other trains".

Network Rail and Greater Thameslink Railway, whose Southern Rail train was involved in the crash, said in a joint statement they were "sorry this happened on our railway".

Investigators from the RAIB have said CCTV from a train which passed through the crash site at 14:04 BST showed the "irregularity" with the track geometry just before the point where the train came off the tracks.

The 14:24 service from London Victoria to Eastbourne derailed in the Landport area of Lewes at about 15:54 BST.

The derailment left two people seriously injured, and 18 were taken to hospital with less serious injuries. The 18 have since left hospital.

News.title: Thunderstorm warnings issued for parts of UK with flash flooding expected
News.content:
Yellow thunderstorm warnings have been issued across the UK, with heavy showers expected to lead to flash flooding and travel disruption.

The Met Office warnings will come into force across northern England, Northern Ireland and eastern Scotland later in the day on Wednesday. The warning for northern England will remain in place until Thursday morning.

The downpours follow almost two months of dry weather, with parts of the country experiencing their first rain in weeks on Tuesday.

People in areas impacted by thunderstorms have been told by the Met Office to expect that businesses and homes could flood, transport services could be delayed and power cuts are likely.

The yellow weather warnings are in place for:

Northern Ireland from 12:00 until 23:59 BST on Wednesday

Parts of North East Scotland, including Aberdeen, from 14:00 until 21:00 on Wednesday

Parts of the North of England, including Manchester and Newcastle upon Tyne, from 19:00 until 10:00 on Thursday

The Met Office said lightning, hail and thunder were expected in the areas affected by warnings, with up to 30mm of rain expected within a few hours in parts of North East Scotland and across Northern Ireland.

Parts of northern England could see up to 50mm of rain within six hours.

Much of the UK has seen a mixture of sunshine and scattered showers already on Wednesday.

In Wisley, Surrey, a 62-day long dry spell was broken on Wednesday morning, with the remarkable run ending after 1.6mm fell before 10.00.

News.title: Salmonella outbreak: What we know so far
News.content:
The UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) has recently declared a national outbreak, external of salmonella food poisoning after one person died and hundreds more fell ill with the bug.

Although not yet proven, imported eggs or dishes containing them are the leading suspects as to the cause.

Evidence also suggests people caught the bug while eating out, rather than at home - with catering and food services such as restaurants, cafes or take-aways likely to play a part.

But there is still a lot to be discovered.

What do we know and what questions remain?

News.title: 'Incredible': SpaceX rocket spotted off Christmas Island coast
News.content:
A SpaceX rocket has made an unexpected appearance off Christmas Island after touching down in the Indian Ocean following a test flight from Texas on 24 July.

David Watchorn, chair of the Christmas Island Tourism Association said he initially thought he was looking at ships on his way to work, before realising it was "a rocket, a space rocket" being towed.

The 52-metre long rocket has caused a stir among locals, with some "sneaking out" of work for a glimpse, and others preparing their boats for a closer look at the debris.

"It's really incredible to think about what it's been through," Watchorn told the BBC.

"The more and more you look at it, the more fascinating it's becoming".

News.title: Students wait for GCSE and BTec  grades as app launches for 750 schools in England
News.content:
Pupils in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will receive GCSE, BTecs and other Level 2 results on Thursday, with some grades in England available through an app that is rolling out for the first time.

Schools and colleges will distribute grades in person, but from 11:00 BST pupils at more than 750 schools in England will also be able to see their grades on their phones.

Results this year come as the government in England plans to boost technical education and address a growing number of English and Maths GCSE resits.

Last year, 67.4% of all GCSE entries were graded 4/C or above.

News.title: BBC presenter Emma Barnett reveals she 'had the hysterectomy I never wanted to have'
News.content:
BBC presenter Emma Barnett has revealed she had a hysterectomy and surgery for endometriosis days before a documentary she made about the condition was broadcast.

Barnett, 41, returned to Radio 4's Today programme on Wednesday morning, explaining she had been absent in recent weeks because she was in hospital "in a case of life imitating work".

She told listeners: "I made a programme on endometriosis on BBC Two and ended up being in hospital for endometriosis.

"So yes, I've been recuperating, shall we say, from surgery for endometriosis and a hysterectomy to boot. So that's been less fun than the Today programme, but it is lovely to be back."

Barnett's announcement came soon after she published a blog about the "hysterectomy I never wanted to have", external.

The presenter, who has two children, said it was "totally surreal" to be in hospital on the night her documentary was broadcast in June, only well enough to watch the final 10 minutes.

"Some 48 hours before the documentary aired - I had undergone a near-5 hour surgery and somehow found myself lying in bed recovering from extensive endometriosis surgery, a hysterectomy and a gallbladder removal," she wrote.

"Triple threat. Go big or go home. Life imitating art."

She added: "I felt blind-sided and robbed, even though my care had been superb and doctors, utterly brilliant.

"But this was not the road I had envisioned for myself. I had the hysterectomy I never wanted to have."

Endometriosis is where cells similar to those in the lining of the womb grow in other parts of the body, resulting in what Barnett has described as "bone-grinding, life-altering pain". It affects one in 10 women and there is no known cure.

A hysterectomy is a surgical procedure to remove the womb (uterus). A hysterectomy alongside removal of endometriosis can reduce the risk of recurrence, according to Endometriosis UK, external.

In her blog, Barnett also said she suspected most of her pain may have been down to another condition, adenomyosis, which can be treated by a hysterectomy.

Her surgery was necessitated after she had an ultrasound while filming the final scene of the documentary, and a problem in her gallbladder was found. "Suddenly things became urgent and non negotiable."

The broadcaster added that she was hopeful that the surgery had helped.

She wrote: "Early indications are that the pain is very much improved - although I am still healing from the surgery itself so that also feels uncertain and frightening to admit - even to myself."

News.title: Murder investigation after woman dies and nine injured in fire in west London
News.content:
A murder investigation is under way after a woman died in a fire in west London, the Metropolitan Police has said.

Officers were called to a residential address on Berkley Avenue, Hounslow, at 01:14 BST following reports of the blaze.

Nine people - six men and three women - were taken to hospital, where the 48-year-old woman died. Another woman, 40, is in a life-threatening condition.

The Met said no arrests had yet been made but officers believed the fire may have been started deliberately. Det Ch Insp Neil John said: "Our inquiries are progressing at pace as we work to establish the full circumstances surrounding the fire."

John said the force's thoughts were "first and foremost with the victim's family and loved ones at this extremely difficult time, as well as everyone who has been injured".

The remaining seven people have been discharged after receiving treatment for minor injuries.

John said the force understood the incident to be isolated to a residential address, but officers would remain in the area and provide updates as the investigation continues.

The London Fire Brigade and London Ambulance Service also attended the scene.
