Sports.title: Liverpool told they spent Mohamed Salah’s wages on the wrong player
Sports.content:
Luis Diaz should have been the Liverpool player that was given a £400,000-a-week contract - not Mohamed Salah.

That's the bold view of ex-Reds midfielder Danny Murphy, who believes the Merseyside outfit have been made to regret selling Diaz.

3 Diaz was a fan favourite during his time at Anfield - winning five trophies Credit: Getty

The 29-year-old spent three-and-a-half-years at Anfield after joining from Porto in January 2022 for £45million.

But despite chipping in with 41 goals and 23 assists in 148 games across all competitions, the winger was sold to Bayern Munich last summer.

Having scored 17 times in the 2024/25 season - helping Liverpool win the Premier League title - he departed in a package deal worth £65.5m.

How much was Salah earning at Liverpool?

Diaz's exit came just three months after Salah penned a lucrative two-year contract extension worth a whopping £400k-per-week.

Less than 12 months later, the 34-year-old announced he would be leaving the club following the conclusion of the 2025/26 campaign on a free transfer.

Salah, who has linked up at Turkish side Trabzonspor, ultimately failed to live up to his previous heroics last term - scoring seven top-flight goals [12 in all competitions] - his lowest return since moving to Liverpool in 2017.

In contrast, Diaz enjoyed the best season of his career to date at the Allianz Arena - firing in 26 goals and supplying 23 assists to help Bayern win the Bundesliga, DFB-Pokal and the Franz Beckenbauer Supercup.

And for Murphy, who won five trophies during his seven-year stay at Liverpool, he insists that Liverpool haven't been able to replace Diaz.

That is despite splashing out £446m on new signings last summer - a record-breaking figure from a single club in a window.

As well as parting ways with Diaz, Liverpool also sold Trent Alexander-Arnold, with fellow club icon Andy Robertson then released earlier this summer after having his minutes reduced for the following season.

3 Wingers Salah and Diaz helped spearhead Liverpool to the Premier League title in 2025 Credit: AFP

What has Danny Murphy said about Liverpool?

Speaking on the White and Jordan show on Wednesday, talkSPORT pundit Murphy commented on Liverpool's struggles last campaign, which saw them finish in fifth spot.

He said: "I think what happened with Liverpool at the beginning of last season [six defeats in opening 12 league game], they lost quality.

"Diaz... I know Salah's numbers were better, but I was one of the few that said, 'I'd rather Diaz stay and give him the money [from Salah's contract].'

"Because Salah was nearing the end, I know the year they won the league, he was a huge contributor [29 league goals].

"But Diaz was a big miss, [a] huge miss.

"And then Trent's gone, and for all the criticism of his defending, from an end product point of view, he was incredible, one of the best full-backs we've seen.

3 Diaz has established himself as one of the world's best forwards since making the move to Germany Credit: Getty

"Robbo [Robertson] got benched, completely unfairly, and actually [Milos] Kerkez struggled.

"So you started taking bits out, and what replaced them wasn't good enough.

"Then the [Alexander] Isak injury, it was a mixture of things.

"What [Andoni] Iraola has got to do in the first couple of months - especially as there's this need and expectation to be successful now and play good football with it.

"He's got to get the fans on board with what they're trying to do, I think he will."

The Iraola era at Liverpool begins against Newcastle at St James' Park on Sunday - a stadium the Reds haven't lost at since December 2015.

Sports.title: Tottenham push on with moves for City duo Marmoush and Savinho, Aston Villa face competition for Tosin Adarabioyo... and Newcastle are offered former Blues forward Christopher Nkunku: WINDOW WATCH
Sports.content:
It's that time of the year again – the transfer window is now open until September 1 and it's sure to be a busy period as clubs look to make big signings ahead of the new season. Here are today's latest developments from Simon Jones and the Daily Mail Sport team... Spurs push on with Marmoush and Savinho swoops Tottenham are continuing negotiations with Manchester City over the double deal of Savinho and Omar Marmoush. As Daily Mail Sport previously revealed, Spurs have identified the Brazilian winger and Egyptian forward as two targets for their forward line along with Liverpool’s Cody Gakpo. The deal with City would not be cheap, however, while coach Enzo Maresca also wants to ensure he has enough bodies with Jeremy Doku out for the start of the season. Liverpool, meanwhile, need to ensure they strengthen their own attacking options before allowing anyone to leave and would want a considerable fee to even consider selling Gakpo. Tottenham have made their interest known. Villa and Marseille keen on Chelsea's Tosin - after he loses No4 shirt Aston Villa hold interest in Chelsea defender Tosin Adarabioyo but face competition from Marseille. Adarabioyo is one of a number of options being considered by Unai Emery. The 6ft 5ins centre-back had been willing to stay at Stamford Bridge and fight for his place but it is becoming apparent it would be in his career's best interests to explore a move away where he would have a more prominent role. Villa have been assessing names throughout the window after it became clear Arsenal would pursue Ezri Konsa who is likely to wrap up his £51m move to the champions by the weekend. Adarabioyo also has other other clubs to consider. Marseille have made contact with Chelsea and are deemed most likely to pursue a move as it stands. Tosin Adarabioyo signs a shirt for a fan in Hong Kong on Chelsea's pre-season tour Sevilla are also keen as are Marco Silva's Benfica but are not considered as strong as Marseille and Villa. Other clubs are also now showing interest in the 28-year-old who joined as a free agent after leaving Fulham in 2024. In another ominous sign, Adarabioyo has also lost his shirt number in a squad list reshuffle. Formerly No 4, Adarabioyo will now wear No 38. New signing Valentin Barco takes his old shirt. Liam Delap is no longer No 9 and will wear No 12,with Joao Pedro taking the No 9. Chslsea bag Hearts' Osborne Chelsea have signed 17-year-old centre-back Alfie Osborne from Hearts for £400,000. Osborne captained Hearts’ U18s to the Scottish FA Youth Cup and has also captained Scotland's U19s. Reijnders seals Saudi move Manchester City midfielder Tijjani Reijnders has joined Al Qadsiah for £52m. Reijnders will work under Brendan Rodgers at Al Qadsiah. The 28-year-old, who has an offer from Nottingham Forest also, only joined City from AC Milan last summer for £46.3m and made 50 appearances, scoring seven goals. Tijjani Reijnders is leaving Manchester City after just one season Clarets land Coudet Burnley have signed goalkeeper Gregoire Coudet from French side Brest on a permanent deal. The 27-year-old has signed a four-year contract. Norwich City have signed Fenerbahce winger Anthony Musaba on a season's loan. The Championship club will pay a proportion of the 25-year-old's salary after finding a replacement for Ali Ahmed following his knee injury. Inter hopeful of £30m deal for Jones Liverpool and Inter Milan have resumed talks over a deal for Curtis Jones today, initiated by the Italian side. There is currently no agreement for the 25-year-old but terms are being discussed. Something in line with the package and structure Inter utilised to sign Tottenham defender Djed Spence - €35m (£30m) - will likely see a deal agreed for the midfielder between the clubs. However, club sources underline these are verbal negotiations at present, and no actual agreement has been reached. Toffees consider Cash grab Everton are showing interest in Aston Villa right back Matty Cash as they assess all options in the market. Villa are signing Aaron Wan-Bissaka from West Ham today and he is being brought in to increase competition for Cash in the right-back berth. Poland international Cash has three years left on contract. Everton have been working through a raft of names to try and solve their issue at right-back which has even prompted questions from Prime Minister Andy Burnham. Barca keep tabs on Kane Barcelona are monitoring Harry Kane's contract talks with Bayern Munich. The England captain is giving priority to resolving his future with the German champions where he is settled and discussions are ongoing about the length of deal for the 33-year-old. Kane is understood to want a three year deal and, as Daily Mail Sport revealed earlier this summer, Barca have made their interest known. Read the full story here. Villa braced for another Watkins bid Aston Villa anticipate a fourth bid from Al Hilal for striker Ollie Watkins. The England international is open to the move but so far Villa have rejected their advances and want to keep the 30-year-old. Aston Villa striker Ollie Watkins is understood to be open to a move to Saudi Arabia The latest bid of £38m was rejected on Tuesday evening. Villa maintain interested in Chelsea's Nicolas Jackson and have confirmed the signings of Matteo Ruggeri and Zion Suzuki. Left back Ruggeri, 24, joins from Atletico Madrid, while goalkeeper Suzuki, 23, arrives after two years in Italy with Parma. Meanwhile, Rangers have signed right back Kosta Nedeljkovic from Villa. The 20-year-old has moved to Ibrox on a season-long loan, with a £4m obligation to buy, which will be triggered by the number of games he plays. As Daily Mail Sport revealed last week, Villa are signing Aaron Wan Bissaka on loan from West Ham pending his medical today. The deal can become an obligation to buy at around £18million. There's a new Cherif in town Coventry have completed their ninth signing of the summer transfer window with Fenerbahce striker Sidiki Cherif for £20.5million. The deal has taken the club's spending to over £120m. The 19-year-old, who was a target for Crystal Palace and Wrexham in January, made appearances in the Europa League and in this season’s Champions League qualifiers prior to opening talks with Coventry. Toon's Nkunku offer Newcastle have been offered the chance to sign former Chelsea forward Christopher Nkunku from AC Milan. However, their priority remains to sign a midfielder first hence talks with Man City for Nico Gonzalez. Other targets are also being discussed. Nkunku has been told he can leave Milan and has interest from RB Leipzig among others. ... and they're closing in on Diabate Newcastle are also closing on Genclerbirligi’s midfielder Ousmane Diabate. The highly-rated 18-year-old had been set for Brentford while Tottenham had also shown interest. However, Newcastle look to have won the race with the teenager likely to stay on loan in Turkey for another season. Diabate, a defensive midfielder, has played 10 matches for the U19s and seven for Genclerbirligi’s first team so far. Liverpool defensive prospect in talks over La Liga move Liverpool defensive prospect Ifeanyi Ndukwe is in talks to join Levante on loan. The 18-year-old does not qualify for a work permit in England so is having to be loaned out. The Austrian youth international has excelled during Liverpool's pre-season and the club have high hopes for his future. First team football in a top league such as La Liga is viewed as an integral next step. He also has interest from Portugal and Germany. Winger Kieran Morrison is joining Sheffield Wednesday on loan today. Liverpool continue to discuss a move for Bradley Barcola at Paris St Germain but a deal for his teammate Ibrahim Mbaye is unlikely. Konsa nearing Arsenal move... Arsenal have agreed a £51million deal plus add-ons for Aston Villa's Ezri Konsa. The England international has said goodbyes to staff at Villa and is due to undergo a medical tomorrow. Read the full story here. As Gunners move for United youngster Arsenal are also working on a deal for 20-year-old right back Habeeb Ogunneye from Manchester United. Arsenal want players to boost their U21s squad and have also shown interest in United's James Scanlon. Gibraltar international winger Scanlon was on loan at Swindon Town last season. England youth international Ogunneye had a spell at Newport on loan. Baleba close to United switch Manchester United are closing on a £65million deal for Brighton midfielder Carlos Baleba. Talks resumed for the Cameroon international in recent weeks after it became apparent his ankle ligament injury was not as serious as first feared. Read the full story here. Pogba tears up Monaco deal Monaco have confirmed that Paul Pogba has left by mutual agreement, bringing his time at the Ligue 1 club to a premature end. The 33-year-old former Manchester United midfielder is now a free agent and has been offered to clubs in the MLS. Read the full story here. Paul Pogba's time at Monaco is over - with MLS clubs now considering a move for the former Man United midfielder Farke reunites with Elvedi Leeds have signed Nico Elvedi from Borussia Monchengladbach. The final fee is £6.5m rising to £8.5m with bonuses. The 29-year-old Switzerland international centre back worked with Daniel Farke previously at the Bundesliga club. James set for Wolves move Rennes midfielder Jordan James is poised to finalise his move to Wolves today pending his medical. The Wales international midfielder is joining on an initial loan deal with an option to sign permanently for around £10m. He impressed on loan at Leicester last season scoring 11 goals in 34 games and had interest from Middlesbrough and West Ham. Chelsea defender closes on Italy move Chelsea defender Benoit Badiashile has arrived at Villa Stuart in Rome ahead of his medical this morning. The 25-year-old centre back is joining Napoli on loan for around £2.5m with an option for the deal to become permanent at £23m. Mamadou Sarr, meanwhile, is emerging as a target for Real Sociedad and Al Hilal. The 20-year-old has been expected to go on loan in the Premier League and interest there remains. The Senegal international was recalled from a loan at Strasbourg to provide cover last season and started in their FA Cup win over Hull. Piroe party at West Ham West Ham have signed Joel Piroe on loan from Leeds until the end of the season. The deal also includes an option for it to become permanent, which will be activated should certain conditions be met, including West Ham winning promotion back to the Premier League. Joel Piroe has joined West Ham on loan from Leeds West Ham turned to 27-year-old Piroe after hitting an impasse in talks for AZ Alkmaar striker Troy Parrott who is joining Real Betis for £17m plus add ons. Piroe, who has scored 73 goals in the Championship during spells with Leeds and Swansea , said: 'I see West Ham as a Club that really wants to be in the Premier League, and I think should be in the Premier League. 'With my experience, I think I can help the Club a lot to achieve what they want to achieve, and I think it’s a good opportunity for me to show what I’ve learnt and how I’ve grown as a football player over the years.' Piroe finished the 2024-25 season as the Championship's top scorer, helping Leeds United earn promotion to the Premier League. The Hammers remain an option for free agent Jamie Vardy. Sports.title: Chelsea Confidential transfer special: The shock Arsenal star on Blues' radar, club insiders reveal change to Enzo Fernandez's price tag, updates on Pedro Neto and Mykhailo Mudryk and the players set to be sold in £500m exodus
Sports.content:
Chelsea are bound to be the busiest Premier League club in what remains of the summer transfer window – at least when it comes to getting players out of the door.

Xabi Alonso does not need a bloated squad with no European football in his first season in charge, and those higher up at Stamford Bridge have less than two weeks to finalise business.

Here, Chelsea Confidential answers your questions on how they are shaping up ahead of their 2026-27 opener away at Fulham, starting with who is in line to leave before the window closes on September 1. Spoiler alert: there are a fair few players.

Who could still leave Chelsea?

In a perfect world where Chelsea get precisely the asking prices they have set, they will do half a billion pound’s worth of sales in this next week or so.

We’ll start with some of the valuations stood up by sources: Nicolas Jackson, £65million; Malo Gusto, £75m; Pedro Neto, close to £100m; Liam Delap, at least £50m; Axel Disasi, £25m; Marc Guiu, £25m. Then there is Enzo Fernandez and his £120m value which will be covered more in depth in the next question.

Add all that together and Chelsea are knocking on £460m alone before getting to the others who could yet leave permanently or temporarily, such as Tosin Adarabioyo, Mamadou Sarr, Aaron Anselmino, Mykhailo Mudryk, Omari Kellyman, David Datro Fofana, Caleb Wiley, Shim Mheuka, Deivid Washington and Benoit Badiashile, who is set to join Napoli on a £3.4m loan with a £23m option. If they all exited, it would easily take Chelsea over the £500m mark.

Xabi Alonso is keen to trim his bloated squad between now and transfer deadline day on September 1

Nicolas Jackson is among the stars who could be on the way out, amid interest from Aston Villa

Except, the market isn’t some magical utopia where asking prices are automatically accepted. Delap’s £50m price is steep for those Premier League clubs who saw his struggles last season. Gusto’s £75m valuation has already scared away some suitors. Neto being valued at close to £100m shows how highly he is appreciated inside Chelsea and could prove problematic for those interested if there is little wiggle room.

Still, the sheer number of names above shows how hectic the end of this window will be for Chelsea. While they have been mocked for having such a large leadership set-up, it is actually helpful that the club have five sporting directors each overseeing their own areas, and a co-owner in Behdad Eghbali who is extremely hands-on unlike others elsewhere, because of the work they tend to get through in these windows.

There are still 42 player profiles listed on Chelsea’s website for their senior squad. Disasi is not even among those shown on there, but it does include the odd academy representative, such as Reggie Walsh, whose loan move to League One Wigan is close to being announced.

Chelsea’s director of finance is called Paul Ramos. He will have been with the club for 25 years as of next month. I can only imagine Ramos and the others in his department will need a stiff drink after sifting through the numbers over this next week or two. I might too.

Will Fernandez stay or go? Has his £120m valuation gone up after Chelsea’s deadline passed?

That’s been the £120m question of the summer. Maybe more than that now, because Chelsea sources speaking confidentially say valuations have indeed increased since they originally set theirs for Fernandez in late May.

It is claimed those terms expired with their deadline at 5pm last Friday. Interestingly, Chelsea insiders have also told me that the money aside, it is now more about strengthening versus weakening the squad for them at this stage. If Fernandez were sold to City now, Chelsea would have limited time to recruit a replacement, and that is a major factor in their thinking.

Because of all that, sources inside Stamford Bridge are saying today that they expect the 25-year-old Argentinian will end up staying. We’ll soon see.

Sources inside Stamford Bridge are saying Chelsea fans can expect Enzo Fernandez to stay put

Is is true Chelsea have enlisted Jorge Mendes to sort Fernandez’s exit?

Chelsea say there is no truth to claims that they have called in the super agent, Jorge Mendes, to help sell Fernandez. Mendes and his Gestifute agency did not respond to a request for comment when contacted. Mendes helped bring Fernandez to Chelsea from Benfica for £106.8m in 2023.

What happens next with Fernandez?

While Chelsea sources are saying he is expected to stay, I would never say never to a sale while the summer window remains open. It all depends. It depends on City and what they are willing to offer and how soon they make any move. It depends on Chelsea and what they are willing to accept and whether they think there is still time to reinvest.

Fernandez is represented by Javier Pastore, the former Paris Saint-Germain midfielder who appears to have lost a few friends this summer by being outspoken on his client’s future.

The terms and conditions for a £120m sale were verbally communicated by Chelsea to Fernandez’s camp at the end of May following their 1-0 league loss at Sunderland which capped a subpar 2025-26. The club then waited for a bid to arrive in June and July – and nothing happened. They then set their own deadline for offers by Friday August 14 at 5pm – and nothing happened. Now the summer is nearly over.

Chelsea would be strengthening a direct rival by agreeing to sell to City and potentially weakening themselves so late in the window. Speaking anonymously, one member of a midfielder’s camp who Chelsea could have targeted as a replacement for Fernandez told us they now do not think the Argentine will be sold as the time for that has passed.

That seems to be the general feeling from those I’ve consulted. We have to wait and see if City change those minds.

If Fernandez is still a Chelsea player come September, I would not even be surprised if we then hear talk of him agreeing new terms, perhaps with a contract which includes a release clause for next summer. Side note: Chelsea are already looking to announce more than one extension in the coming weeks, with Joao Pedro among those in line for a boost.

Talented forward Joao Pedro is set to sign a contract extension in the coming weeks

Who could Chelsea target if they sell Fernandez?

The time for recruiting a replacement may be running out, but there are contenders should Fernandez be sold.

Chelsea have already bid for Bournemouth’s Alex Scott once this summer. They offered £64m for the 22-year-old midfielder in mid-July. Bournemouth rejected it, and reiterated that he is not for sale and has no set valuation. Chelsea haven’t suddenly stopped liking Scott because of that stance.

Adam Wharton, also 22, has long been linked and there is admiration for him. However, Crystal Palace would not let him leave on the cheap, and Chelsea have already attempted to play down those links this summer.

One new name I have heard is Martin Zubimendi, though recent checks at Arsenal suggested the 27-year-old is expected to stay at the Emirates Stadium. Alonso is a fan of Zubimendi and vice versa. They worked together at Real Sociedad B. They nearly teamed up again at Real Madrid. They share the same agent.

Daily Mail Sport also reported this week how Chelsea showed interest in Morgan Gibbs-White earlier in this window, though Nottingham Forest have insisted publicly and privately that he is not for sale.

Xabi Alonso admires Arsenal midfielder Martin Zubimendi, and the feeling is mutual

Best guess at a Chelsea XI for Fulham? And back three or four?

Here’s my stab involving the players currently available. Chelsea (3-4-2-1): Sanchez; James, Lacroix, Colwill; Neto, Fernandez, Caicedo, Palestra; Palmer, Rogers; Joao Pedro.

As has been the case in Chelsea’s eight pre-season friendlies, I suspect Alonso will switch between a three and a four, depending on what he decides is best, game by game. He should have plenty of time to work on team structure at Cobham.

The calendar shows Chelsea aren't set to leave London until Everton away in the Premier League on October 17 – unless they beat Luton in the Carabao Cup and draw a club out of the capital for the following round, that is.

Will Chelsea sign another centre back?

Alonso told us he wants ‘four or five' centre backs while we were in Sydney, Australia. When Chelsea signed Maxence Lacroix, they had 10 in total.

Trevoh Chalobah has already been sold to Como, and Disasi and Badiashile should soon leave also. Tosin has interest from clubs in England and Europe – Benfica, managed by Marco Silva, formerly of Fulham, are among them – and Sarr likewise has options. If all those depart, that would leave five in Lacroix, Levi Colwill, Wesley Fofana, Josh Acheampong, and Anselmino, who impressed in pre-season before picking up an unfortunate hamstring injury during a 3-3 draw with Johor Darul Ta'zim.

Are Chelsea in for Emi Martinez? Who is the No 1 goalkeeper?

Chelsea and Aston Villa do have a good relationship, so it’s a natural link to make, but I haven't heard of any talks for Martinez after his move to Juventus fell through. Privately and publicly, Chelsea and Alonso have reiterated several times this summer that they are more than satisfied with Robert Sanchez and Mike Penders as their one-two.

Alonso indicated to us during the tour that owing to his experience, Sanchez will start as his No 1. My guess is Sanchez will be in goal versus Fulham in the Premier League opener, then perhaps we will see Penders against Luton in the Carabao Cup.

As for Villa, I could still see them making their move for Jackson, though they face competition from others in England and Europe. Jackson is one of those players whose valuation from Chelsea – £65m – is more than fair in my eyes.

I haven't heard any talk about Chelsea making a move for Emi Martinez - my guess is Robert Sanchez (pictured) will start the season as No1

Why are Chelsea pricing Neto out of a move?

Chelsea class Neto as an elite winger, and they value him highly enough to say they would want close to £100m to consider a sale this summer. Sources have said several times this summer that the prices of proven wide men have spiked in this window.

Chelsea did not want to place an asking price on Neto when I asked last month, but they did tell me they were tracking the market, and particularly the situations involving Yan Diomande, who joined Real Madrid from RB Leipzig for a fee worth up to £120m, and Bradley Barcola, valued at north of £100m by PSG.

Neto was used at right wing-back in Chelsea’s last friendly win over Real Sociedad, and while the 26-year-old performed well, it may not be his favoured position if Alonso wants to regularly use a 3-4-2-1 set-up. I have not heard that Neto has directly communicated a desire to leave Chelsea. He will still be one to watch in the build-up to September.

What happens with Mudryk?

I wrote a story two weeks ago that as soon as his suspension was lifted, Chelsea received multiple enquiries as to their plans for Mudryk for this season. Surprisingly so. Because nobody knew Mudryk’s level after so long out of the game. Not even Chelsea.

They flew him out to Hong Kong to join their pre-season tour so he could be assessed by Alonso and Co. I also wrote in that story above that three Premier League clubs enquired with Chelsea, and one of those was Coventry, managed by Frank Lampard.

Mykhailo Mudryk has attracted loan interest from at least three Premier League clubs, including Frank Lampard's Coventry

Strasbourg have always been another safe option if Chelsea want to make sure he gets game time. I think we will see him leave on loan. Chelsea should receive a nice loan fee and have a considerable chunk of his wages covered, but more than that, those inside Stamford Bridge want to make sure the 25-year-old Ukrainian has the best support possible after what he went through.

Playing regular football again would help his confidence, and that may be better found away from Chelsea in the coming season.

Prediction for this season?

Internally, Chelsea’s minimum target is to finish in the top four and to see where that takes them from there. Perhaps this is a tad optimistic, but I’ll predict they place second in the Premier League once 2026-27 is over, above Enzo Maresca's Manchester City and below Mikel Arteta’s Arsenal.

Sports.title: Curtis Jones edging towards £30m transfer from Liverpool to Inter Milan - as the third member of Italian giants' English revolution this summer
Sports.content:
Curtis Jones edging towards £30m transfer from Liverpool to Inter Milan - as the third member of Italian giants' English revolution this summer

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Inter Milan are on the verge of signing Liverpool midfielder Curtis Jones after a summer-long back and forth.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

And it now appears he will leave, with the two clubs in dialogue. A fee of around £30million will get the deal done, with Inter signaling they are ready to pay it.

The Italian champions had a bid of around £21m turned down earlier in the summer and, if they sign Jones, he will be the third Englishman they have bought this window after Manchester City's John Stones and Tottenham's Djed Spence.

Liverpool meanwhile are preparing for their first season under new manager Andoni Iraola, who replaced Arne Slot following the Dutchman's dismissal at the end of last season.

The six-time England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield

It appears Jones will follow Tottenham's Djed Spence as an Englishman heading to Inter

John Stones also moved to the San Siro on a free transfer from Manchester City this summer

The Italian press expect an official announcement on Jones to follow within 'hours' and say a medical has already been scheduled for him.

After spending over £450million on new signings including Alexander Isak, Florian Wirtz and Hugo Ekitike last summer, the 2024-25 Premier League champions struggled to reach the same heights again under the Dutchman and only narrowly managed to qualify for the Champions League with a fifth-place finish last term.

Liverpool, who waved farewell to Mohamed Salah, Andrew Robertson and Ibrahima Konate at the start of the summer, have so far recruited centre-half Jeremy Jacquet from Stade Rennais and left winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna ahead of the new campaign.

While theoretically all first-team places are up for grabs under new boss Iraola, Jones has been viewed as a squad player at the club in recent seasons, playing second fiddle to fellow central midfielders Dominik Szoboszlai, Alexis Mac Allister, Ryan Gravenberch and Wirtz under Slot and previously Jurgen Klopp.

Sports.title: Chelsea launch new outcast training group of stars working separately to team-mates ahead of potential exits - as Blues look to trim squad
Sports.content:
Chelsea have created a second training group who are working separately to Xabi Alonso’s main squad, including Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson ahead of their potential departures.

Both Delap and Jackson could yet leave this summer either permanently or temporarily, while Mykhailo Mudryk has also participated in these alternative sessions with the 25-year-old Ukrainian available for a loan after his suspension from football for anti-doping offences ended.

Chelsea have attempted to get away from the ‘bomb squad’ accusations which have plagued the Premier League club in past years.

This time, they are allowing this second group to work at the same time and on the same training pitch and use the same first-team facilities.

Raheem Sterling was previously among those who had to work on his own at their Cobham headquarters.

Chelsea sources have described it as a fluid group with players coming and going, depending on workloads and what Alonso wants in his main session, and deny any suggestion that only those up for sale or loan have been training separately.

Chelsea have created a second training group that is working separately to Xabi Alonso’s main squad

The group includes several stars who may depart like Liam Delap and Nicolas Jackson (left)

Danny Welbeck and Jordan Henderson have been involved in these other sessions as they get up to speed, for example, along with younger players.

After loaning Reggie Walsh to League One Wigan on Wednesday, Chelsea’s website now lists 41 player profiles for their senior squad.

That does not include Axel Disasi, who has also been working separately from Alonso’s sessions while he works on securing his exit.

Tosin Adarabioyo, who has interest from England and Europe, is also believed to have been with this second group.

Enzo Fernandez, Malo Gusto and Pedro Neto, who have all been linked with leaving and valued at £120million, £75m and close to £100m respectively, have been training with Alonso’s main group.

Chelsea are working on slimming their bloated squad before their 2026-27 season officially starts, with Alonso’s first Premier League fixture in charge coming away at Fulham this Monday.

Sports.title: Referees chief Howard Webb slams FIFA over Folarin Balogun red card scandal
Sports.content:
Referees chief Howard Webb slams FIFA over Folarin Balogun red card scandal

See more Daily Mail on Google - save us as a Preferred Source

Refs' boss Howard Webb has piled into FIFA over the World Cup scandal of Folarin Balogun’s suspended red-card ban.

England’s head of officiating said he was ‘really troubled’ by the saga, which marred the summer’s showpiece.

US striker Balogun was shown a red card in the co-host’s round of 32 victory over Bosnia, which triggered an automatic one-match ban.

However, after the extraordinary and unprecedented intervention of US president Donald Trump, FIFA decided to suspend the ban for 12 months, meaning he was free to play in the last-16 fixture with Belgium.

The saga prompted claims of corruption, with the integrity of the global competition significantly undermined.

‘I was really troubled by it,’ Webb said. ‘We know that there was pressure placed by a politician onto FIFA because that was admitted, and we know that the suspension was taken away for that particular tournament and suspended through a process which seemingly didn't exist before the season the tournament started.’

Donald Trump called FIFA chief Gianni Infantino to ask him to review Folarin Balogun's sending off at the World Cup

The striker was sent off for this challenge during their 2-0 win over Bosnia but his suspension was overturned

Speaking ahead of the new season, Webb added that the move could now spark unfair conspiracy theories across the game.

‘Where I was troubled by it was that we live in a world now which is different to the one that I occupied as a ref, in that decisions that are taken previously were viewed as correct or incorrect,’ he explained.

‘Far too often now, decisions are viewed as correct or corrupt by people who want to type all over social media. They try to draw inferences around decisions around decisions, but they don't agree with them. What's the motivation behind that decision?

‘When you get that type of situation, it opens up space for people to think, “Ha ha! You see, this sort of thing's happening all the time behind the scenes”, and it's really not, in my experience.’

Webb’s comments were echoed by Premier League boss Richard Masters. ‘We should be looking back on the World Cup and the football that was played, and Spain being obviously the best team, and England’s agonising semi-final defeat,’ he said.

‘But we’re not, we are talking about other issues, and I think that’s a huge shame. The Balogun issue stands alone in that isolated incident which is very difficult to comprehend when you look at it. I think it is, again, a self-inflicted moment.’

Meanwhile, Webb said that Pro Ref had increased support to referees following the situation with disgraced former official David Coote, who was given a suspended jail sentence after pleading guilty to making an indecent image of a child.

They have brought in a head of performance psychology, along with a robust reporting process in which any concerns can be raised.

Sports.title: Championship club Sheffield United at risk of 12-point deduction - with owners' company hit by winding-up order - as EFL investigate damaging breaches of rules
Sports.content:
Sheffield United are in danger of a 12-point deduction after the company its owners used to buy the club was hit with a winding up order.

Blades fans will now face an anxious wait, with the EFL investigating whether there has been a potentially damaging breach of its rules.

United World, the investment arm of former owner Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, took COH Sports Bidco to the High Court, claiming it was owed £35m from the sale, which took place in 2024.

It argued that current custodians of the Championship side, American duo Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen, had effectively attempted to take the club without paying for it, after they transferred their shares in United to a new company.

While the Americans dismissed the move as a ‘publicity stunt’, a judge issued the winding up order and the EFL will now decide whether to take further action.

Sheffield United face a nervous wait to see if they are handed a points deduction

A United World spokesperson said it had ‘made every effort to resolve the matter amicably’ and had tried to do so again this morning ‘to give the owners a final opportunity to spare Sheffield United the consequences of their actions’.

‘It appears that Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen are simply not concerned about what this means for the club,’ it added.

‘What happens now is the result of their choices. United World will continue to pursue the full sums.’

A Sheffield United spokesperson said: 'Sheffield United Football Club is aware of today’s hearing at the High Court. This is a matter between the current owners and former owner.

'The Football Club is in contact with the EFL and the day-to-day operations at Sheffield United are unaffected.'

An EFL spokesperson, meanwhile, added: ‘The EFL notes the High Court’s decision to issue a winding up order on COH Sports Bidco Limited. The League will consider the implications of that development in line with its Regulations, including whether any further action is required.

‘In addition, the EFL continues to consider other regulatory matters following changes to the club’s ownership structure and developments within the wider group. As these issues remain ongoing, the EFL will make no further comment at this stage.’

Sports.title: Liverpool Confidential transfer special: The target sources insist is 'all in' on Reds move, update on Ibrahim Mbaye and the young midfielders who have won over Andoni Iraola, revealed by LEWIS STEELE
Sports.content:
Liverpool Confidential transfer special: The target sources insist is 'all in' on Reds move, update on Ibrahim Mbaye and the young midfielders who have won over Andoni Iraola, revealed by LEWIS STEELE

Unlock more from Lewis Steele inside the Liverpool camp with a DailyMail+ subscription - brilliant exclusives, in-depth insight, analysis and more

Liverpool still have a huge to-do list in the transfer market if they are to lay the foundations for a successful season.

The window closes at 11pm on Tuesday, September 1, which means there is now less than a fortnight for the Reds to do, well, a lot of business.

Top of the shopping list is a wide forward to replace Mohamed Salah, while they could also recruit a second winger.

Liverpool have had a quiet summer so far, with the only additions £34.5million winger Victor Munoz from Osasuna, and defender Ronald Araujo, on loan from Barcelona for the season.

Jeremy Jacquet did, however, arrive this summer after his £60m move from Rennes was agreed in January. For what it is worth, the finances of that deal will count on this year’s accounts, taking their summer spend to just north of £100m.

But what else is left to do? Daily Mail Sport's Merseyside expert Lewis Steele answers the big questions...

Andoni Iraola's squad could still do with plenty of additions with just a few weeks to go in the transfer window

The Reds look particularly light on the wing, despite the £35million signing of Victor Munoz from Osasuna

What's going on with the winger pursuit?

Bradley Barcola is desperate to join Liverpool, according to sources. The Paris Saint-Germain and France forward is said to be ‘all in’ on making this move happen.

He has been the top target for some time, going back to when RB Leipzig turned down an £86m approach for winger Yan Diomande, who has since joined Real Madrid for roughly £120m.

PSG have been stubborn over their valuation of Barcola, though. The French and European champions value him at around £145m, which Liverpool view as too high.

PSG have forwards aplenty, having signed Mika Godts from Ajax, World Cup hero Ferran Torres from Barcelona and Maghnes Akliouche from Monaco.

Akliouche, while we are on the topic, is another Liverpool had a look at earlier in the summer but it was always clear the young Frenchman fancied a move to Paris.

These incomings could see PSG soften their valuation of Barcola, with Liverpool also previously on the tail of 18-year-old team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye.

Bradley Barcola (left) is desperate to join Liverpool and has been the top target for some time

So, could they sign both Barcola AND Mbaye?

The Barcola chase is straightforward. Liverpool want him, he wants Liverpool, PSG will do a deal if the price is right.

Mbaye, however, is less clear-cut – and there are two sides to the story.

Reports in French newspapers suggested on Tuesday that he has an agreement to join Liverpool. This has been played down by sources in England, who insist that interest was merely exploratory.

The signings of Munoz and Araujo accelerated quickly, so perhaps that could happen again. For example, Liverpool first made contact with Araujo’s camp four days before he flew to England for his medical.

What we do know is that Liverpool will likely begin the season with wing options of Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha and Munoz, with the out-of-favour Federico Chiesa and young Lewis Koumas lurking in the background.

Two more wingers, especially with Gakpo subject to interest from Tottenham, would certainly be welcome. Maybe the dominoes will soon start to fall…

Reporting in France and sources in England differ in their view of Liverpool's pursuit of Ibrahim Mbaye (right)

Will Liverpool sign a midfielder?

Curtis Jones is on the verge of joining Inter for around £30m after a summer-long back and forth.

The England international, who joined Liverpool aged nine, has had his heart set on a move to Serie A for some time after failing to regularly establish himself as a starter at Anfield.

The Italian champions had a bid of around £21m turned down earlier in the summer and, if they sign Jones, he will be the third Englishman they have bought this window after John Stones and Djed Spence.

Will they sign a midfielder to replace Jones? As it stands, no – though that could change if a deal becomes available in the last week of the market.

Crystal Palace’s Adam Wharton has long been linked with a move but the Selhurst Park club would want a huge fee of around £100m – and there is no indication Liverpool are interested anyway.

Many other midfielders have been mooted but it seems more likely than not that the Reds do not sign a midfielder this window.

That would mean two youngsters will be promoted. Trey Nyoni, who excelled in pre-season and was perhaps Liverpool’s stand-out player on the American tour, is pushing for more minutes and looks more than capable. The 19-year-old has also had plenty of interest.

It is understood James McConnell’s loan move to Championship side Preston has been kiboshed – for now at least – by Liverpool in the last days despite regular game-time being promised.

North End had a deal agreed and met the player but Liverpool pulled the plug.

James McConnell's proposed loan to Preston was cancelled by Liverpool, with McConnell having impressed Iraola

The young midfielder, who spent time at Ajax last season, knocked on the door of boss Andoni Iraola last Friday and was told he is part of his plans after impressing in training and there will be minutes for him in the first team this year.

McConnell also had a meeting with sporting director Richard Hughes, who stressed there is no official pecking order in the midfield so both Nyoni and McConnell can push for minutes.

Will they recoup any money?

Alexis Mac Allister was linked with Real Madrid but nothing was forthcoming and his father, Carlos, has publicly denied any talks with other clubs. Mac Allister has two years remaining on his deal and no new contract is on the table.

The sale of Jones represents a good cash injection, especially for a player with just one year remaining on his deal.

There is also the Gakpo conundrum, with Spurs sniffing around.

Harvey Elliott has failed to take his chance in pre-season after returning from a year to forget at Aston Villa. Some of that might be to do with the fact he has barely played in the last 12 months and his fitness level is not where it should be.

Chiesa started the US tour well with a goal against Sunderland. Speaking after that, he said he was committed to the club and wanted to prove people wrong. But there are a few clubs monitoring his situation and, as ever, Chiesa’s future looks uncertain.

Federico Chiesa has long been out of favour at Liverpool and his future is uncertain

Any other loans?

Young defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe is on the verge of joining La Liga outfit Levante on a season-long loan.

The 18-year-old has been a revelation in pre-season, playing regularly at the heart of defence and winning praise from Iraola.

But Ndukwe does not have a work permit due to a complex new set of regulations. He signed from Austria Vienna in January.

Levante are set to win the race ahead of multiple other clubs across Europe. Liverpool will review the loan in January, by which point he should have the required points to play in England.

Kieran Morrison is on the verge of a loan to Sheffield Wednesday, who are racing to get the winger registered in time to make their squad to face Bradford on Thursday night.

Koumas has a queue of clubs wanting to take him on loan. But his future is less clear-cut as, like McConnell, Iraola has taken a shine to him in pre-season and he could be asked to stick around.

Defender Ifeanyi Ndukwe is set to move on loan to Levante and is a player to keep an eye on

The former Hull, Birmingham and Stoke loanee, son of former Premier League midfielder Jason, could see his situation change if Liverpool were to be busy in terms of incomings.

Defender Luke Chambers also has suitors but it is believed he will not go on loan for the sake of it. Iraola likes the 22-year-old, who excelled on loan at Charlton last season and can play centre half and left back.

Calvin Ramsay is another on the list of potential exits, with St Mirren tracking him, though fellow full back Owen Beck is set to stay after a setback in his recovery from injury.

Sports.title: Tennis bad boy Nick Kyrgios tests positive for cocaine as he reveals his secret ban and will 'step away from public life to get myself right'
Sports.content:
Former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios has been banned from tennis after testing positive for cocaine.

The 31-year-old submitted a sample while playing in Mallorca on June 22 that contained benzoylecgonine, a substance found in the class A drug.

Kyrgios said he took ‘full responsibility’ for his mistake and was ‘deeply disappointed’ in himself.

The Australian has been suspended since August 4, meaning he cannot play in, coach at, or attend any professional men’s or women’s tournament, including Grand Slams such as Wimbledon.

Kyrgios can appeal against the provisional ban, which could see him face between three months and four years on the sidelines.

His ban could also be reduced if he can prove that he did not take the substance for performance-enhancing benefits.

The Australian was the runner-up at Wimbledon in 2022 – his only Grand Slam final to date – losing to Novak Djokovic but won the men's doubles at the Australian Open in the same year.

He has battled knee and wrist injuries in recent years that have seen him make limited appearances at major tournaments.

Kyrgios, who was once the 13th highest-ranked player in the world, announced his suspension in a lengthy statement on Instagram today.

The post read: 'I wanted you to hear it from me first. I recently failed a drug test in Mallorca after testing positive for cocaine.

'I made a huge mistake and I take full responsibility for it.

'I am sorry to my fans, my family, my sponsors, and everyone close to me. Above all, I'm sorry to the kids who follow me. I know the example this sets and I'm deeply disappointed in myself.

'I'm not going to make excuses, but I do want to give some context about where I've been. The last couple of years of injuries have taken a huge toll on me, both physically and mentally. My body hasn't been able to do what my mind expects it to do, and coming to terms with being near the end of my career has been harder than I ever imagined.

Former Wimbledon finalist Nick Kyrgios has been banned from tennis after testing positive for cocaine

The former world No 13 in Brisbane, Australia, in January... he has endured a series of disappointing seasons due to injuries

'I've always said I didn't choose tennis - tennis chose me. But letting go of something that has been my whole life is one of the hardest things I've ever had to face. At times I've felt helpless and alone.

'None of that excuses what I did.

'However, the good news is that this has given me a wake-up call. For the next 28 days, I'll be stepping away from social media and public life while I focus on getting myself right.

'I'd ask that people respect my privacy during that time, and most importantly the privacy of my family.

'I'm sorry. I'll do the work and come back better. Nick.'

Kyrgios played in Majorca at the Association of Tennis Professionals 250 event in late June, losing his singles match to fellow Australian Adam Walton in straight sets on June 22.

He later withdrew from the doubles, where he and partner John-Patrick Smith had been due to play Austin Krajicek and Nikola Mektic the following day.

The International Tennis Integrity Agency (ITIA), the sport's anti-doping body, has since announced that Kyrgios has been handed a mandatory provisional suspension.

A statement read: 'The International Tennis Integrity Agency has provisionally suspended Australian tennis player Nick Kyrgios under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme.

'Kyrgios provided a sample during an ATP 250 event in Mallorca, Spain, on June 22, 2026. On July 17, 2026, a World Anti-Doping Agency (WADA)-accredited laboratory confirmed the presence of benzoylecgonine, a metabolite of cocaine.

'Cocaine is a stimulant and substance of abuse on the WADA Prohibited List and is banned in competition under the Tennis Anti-Doping Programme. If taken out of competition, reduced sanctions apply for substances of abuse.

Kyrgios was the runner-up at Wimbledon in 2022 - his only Grand Slam final to date - losing to Novak Djokovic

'Because of the nature of the substance, a provisional suspension is mandatory and has been in place since August 4, 2026.

'Kyrgios, who reached a career-high world singles ranking of 13 in October 2016, has the right to appeal the provisional suspension, but has not done so to date.

'As with all Tennis Anti-Doping Programme cases, ITIA support is available to Kyrgios.

'While suspended, Kyrgios is not allowed to play in, coach at, or attend any events organised or sanctioned by World Tennis, WTA, ATP, the Grand Slams, or any national association.'

Before his suspension, Kyrgios's appearances on the professional tour had been limited, with the Australian star only taking part in a clutch of events due to his ranking of 919.

He has not won a singles match since last year's Miami Open but has been offered wildcard entries at both singles and doubles events.

Former British star Dan Evans was handed a one-year ban in 2017 after testing positive for cocaine at the Barcelona Open.

The drug had been found in the pocked of his washbag but the International Tennis Federation accepted his explanation that he had been contaminated after the drug found its way onto his finger or medication in the bag accidentally.

Kyrgios's case represents the second high-profile anti-doping revelation in tennis in recent months, after 2023 Wimbledon champion Marketa Vondrousova was handed a four-year ban in June for refusing to take a drugs test.

Sports.content:
1.50 Sky Bet Lowther Stakes - WILD BLOSSOM looks ready for the step up to six furlongs - and the return to Group company.

Racing's 300,000-guinea breeze-up purchase could hardly have got her career off to a better start than when running away with a novice stakes for fillies at Carlisle in May by 10 lengths from subsequent Listed winner Crownbreaker.

Given her trainer Karl Burke’s depth of two-year-old talent, it was no surprise to see the daughter of sent off at just 7-1 for the Group 2 Queen Mary Stakes at Royal Ascot next time. But a draw in stall seven did for Wild Blossom’s chances and, under the circumstances, a 10th-of-27 finish, just over four lengths behind winner Victorious, could have been a lot worse.

Plus, grab a £2 free shop bet inside Thursday and Friday's paper too! ‌



Burke then sent James Doyle’s partner to Glorious Goodwood for the Alice Keppel Fillies' Conditions Stakes and the retrieval mission went to plan as Wild Blossom got back to winning ways with a length-and-a-half defeat of Fast Track.

Although she has raced exclusively at the minimum trip, my selection shouldn’t be troubled by tackling an easy six today and has the untapped potential to make an impression at Group 2 level. Libertango , winner of Royal Ascot’s Group 3 Albany Stakes, is likely to have a say in proceedings, while Star Of State and In The Black are others who merit a second look.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 WILD BLOSSOM, 2 LIBERTANGO, 3 IN THE BLACK

View 7 Images Sun Goddess: Newsboy's tip (Image: Brian Lawless/PA Wire)

‌



2.25 Harry's Half Million By Goffs - SUN GODDESS, as a Group 1 winner, is emphatically the clubhouse leader.

Having come home strongly on her debut to force a dead-heat for second behind Aidan O’Brien stablemate Carry The Flag at Naas in May, Sioux Nation’s daughter duly went one better with a five-length supremacy at the Curragh 15 days later.

Sun Goddess went off the 10-11 favourite for the Group 3 Albany Stakes at Royal Ascot next time and Ryan Moore’s mount led her 24 rivals passing the half-furlong marker, only to be gunned down late on by one-length winner Libertango.

Undeterred, punters backed the Ballydoyle juvenile into 2-7 for the Group 2 Airlie Stud Stakes back at the Curragh just eight days on and they duly got their return, a three-quarter-length margin from Green Empress being scant reflection of the favourite’s superiority.

‌



That success made an ascent to the highest level the next logical move and Sun Goddess returned to the ‘Home of the Irish Classics’ for the Phoenix Stakes last Sunday week, beating Folsom Blues by a length and a quarter.

There’s a 7lb penalty to carry here but Sun Goddess sets the standard the others have to aim for and is expected to go in again. Tokaido is putting together a tidy CV in France and is feared, in company with Satellite Of Love and Vollering.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 SUN GODDESS, 2 TOKAIDO, 3 VOLLERING

View 7 Images Hamad Al Jehani: trains Newsboy's pick (Image: PA)

‌



3.00 Sir Kevin Sinfield 7 in 7 Grand Finale Handicap - BLUE BROTHER didn’t come up to expectations at Glorious Goodwood but is worth another chance.

Only 3-1 favourite Indalo preceded the Hamad Al Jehani-saddled five-year-old in the betting for the 18-runner Golden Mile on the South Downs - Blue Brother went off the 5-1 second choice.

Leading early on under James Doyle, the gelded son of Intello raced in second before fading through the final furlong to pass the post in eighth place behind his winning stablemate Archivist.

A reproduction of that form will send his backers home with empty pockets, but Blue Brother is better judged on his stable debut, and first outing for exactly a year, at Royal Ascot the previous month.

‌



Backed into 9-2 joint-favouritism for the seven-furlong Buckingham Palace Handicap, Blue Brother raced with enthusiasm and finished with gusto to take fourth, beaten two necks and three-quarters of a length, behind Mezcala.

Rain wouldn’t be an issue for a horse who has scored on heavy ground and, with the decision to stay at a mile almost certainly the correct one, Blue Brother is well capable of showing to the fore.

In an open heat, defending champion Bullet Point was back to form at the Shergar Cup and has podium claims, along with The Lost King and Arctic Dawn.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 BLUE BROTHER, 2 THE LOST KING, 3 ARCTIC DAWN

‌



View 7 Images Johanna Walsh: Newsboy's tip in the Yorkshire Oaks (Image: Niall Carson/PA Wire)

3.35 Legend Global Yorkshire Oaks - JOHANNA WALSH is the value alternative to hot favourite Kalpana.

Joseph O’Brien hasn’t taken long to establish himself as a major player at the highest level, and the same can be said of Johanna Walsh.

Third in fillies’ maidens at Thurles and Gowran Park either side of the seasonal break, Sea The Stars’ daughter made it third time lucky with a three-and-a-quarter-length supremacy in a similar event at Leopardstown before her sights were raised to Group level.

‌



First up was the Group 2 Ribblesdale Stakes at Royal Ascot, for which my selection went off at 9-1 in a field of 12.

Never far from the action under Dylan Browne McMonagle, Johanna Walsh straightened for home in front but was unable to resist the late thrust of Earth Shot, who took the spoils by a head.

The pair reopposed in the Irish Oaks at the Curragh a month later but this time it was Johanna Walsh who came out on top, moving smoothly into the lead two furlongs out before shooting four lengths clear of Inis Mor, with Sparan Nua third and Earth Shot only sixth.

That emphatic triumph is unlikely to be Johanna Walsh last in the top tier, especially with more to come on the sixth start of her life.

‌



Kalpana comes here on the back of a thrilling King George VI And Queen Elizabeth Stakes success and is greatly respected, with defending champion Minnie Hauk and Legacy Link also in the mix.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 JOHANNA WALSH, 2 KALPANA, 3 INIS MOR

View 7 Images John Gosden: co-trainer of Morrophore (Image: David Davies/PA Wire)

4.10 British EBF & Sir Henry Cecil Galtres Stakes - MORROPHORE, taking on Listed opposition on her first start for seven months, is interesting.

‌



Nobody would describe the Kingman mare, trained in tandem by John and Thady Gosden, as equine poetry in motion - Morrophore flashes her tail and can look unwilling under pressure.

But only a hard audience would deny the five-year-old is a progressive performer - she has won four of her eight races, with the promise of better to come.

Unraced at two, Morrophore landed a novice stakes for fillies at Wolverhampton as a three-year-old in October 2024, doubling up in the handicap sphere at Ascot the following May.

Ryan Moore’s mount put a third win on her CV with a half-length call in the Winter Oaks Trial Fillies’ Handicap over 10 furlongs at Lingfield Park last December. And she returned to Surrey to capture the real thing in January, arriving just in the nick of time to shade Sky Safari by a head.

‌



Although she takes a rise in class, Morrophore is the best horse in this race according to the British Horseracing Authority figures and the fact she is a half-sister to three winners over a mile and a half augurs well for this step up in distance.

A La Prochaine, a 10-length fourth to Thundering On in the Oaks on her latest outing, is taken to fight it out with Vauntingly and Sunshine Star for the minor medals.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 MORROPHORE, 2 A LA PROCHAINE, 3 VAUNTINGLY

View 7 Images George Boughey: trainer of Mirzimaan (Image: PA)

‌



4.45 Mews Hotel Ossett EBF Stallions Nursery Handicap - MIRZIMAAN receives the vote to prove well treated as he makes his debut in the handicap milieu.

There is plenty to like about my selection’s pedigree - sire Mohaather was a Group 1-winning miler while dam Altaayshah didn’t make it to the track but is a sister to star sprinter Battaash. His blue-blooded ancestry counted for nothing when Mirzimaan trailed home last of 13 when a 16-1 chance for a six-furlong novice stakes at Newmarket in May.

But my selection clearly learned plenty from that experience - 55 days later, Mirzimaan took on 17 opponents for a similar event at Newbury and beat them all, containing Minster Boy by a length and a quarter.

And he was unlucky not to follow up under a penalty at Newcastle on his most recent outing, finding plenty of trouble in running before he steamed home for a short-head second to Asander.

‌



The step up from six furlongs to seven is a plus, and an opening British Horseracing Authority mark of 82 there for the taking. Dangers lurk at every turn in this full-field nursery, with Perfect Nation, Revels, Bymiddaytomorrow and Telegraphic just four juveniles whose best days lie ahead of them.

View 7 Images Oisin Orr (centre); rides Newsboy's selection (Image: Bahrain Turf Club/Racingfotos.com)

5.20 British EBF Fillies' Handicap - OOLONG POOBONG looks up to rewarding each-way support - at the very least.

A fine fourth in the Sandringham Fillies’ Handicap at Royal Ascot in June 2025 proved to be the Ed Bethell-trained daughter of Make Believe’s final start of last season. Oolong Poobong has met with defeat in both outings during the current campaign, but that doesn’t tell the whole story.

‌



She was entitled to come on for her reappearance, a perfectly respectable fifth at Thirsk in mid-May, after an absence of 330 days.

And a stall-three draw for the Kensington Palace Handicap for fillies and mares at Royal Ascot effectively snuffed out her chance - Jamie Spencer steered a path over to the stands’ side but Oolong Poobong couldn’t get involved, coming home in 20th.

Oisin Orr’s mount is better than she has been able to show so far this year and the step back from a mile won’t be a hindrance for a filly whose two career successes have been at six and seven furlongs. Oolong Poobong’s stablemate Caim, Secret History and and the returning Lam Yai all have something to recommend them.

NEWSBOY’S 1-2-3: 1 OOLONG POOBONG, 2 SECRET HISTORY, 3 CAIM

Sports.title: Premier League 3pm TV blackout could get SCRAPPED with talks to be held over streaming
Sports.content:
Premier League 3pm TV blackout could get SCRAPPED with talks to be held over streaming

The Premier League and EFL 3pm blackout could be in the process of getting scrapped with talks to be held ahead of a final decision

View 2 Images The Premier League 3pm blackout could be scrapped (Image: Getty Images)

Premier League chief executive Richard Masters has revealed a decision on ending the 3pm blackout could be made before the end of the 2027/28 season.

‌



Currently, top-flight matches in England cannot be broadcast live on live domestic television between 2.45pm and 5.15pm on a Saturday afternoon. The tradition, which was enforced by the FA at the request of the EFL in the 1960s, is known as the '3pm blackout'.

‌



But there is talk that it could be removed when the next TV rights deal is finalised in 2028. The current cycle is due to expire at the end of the 2028/29 season. With that, a potential removal of the blackout would not be able to be introduced until the start of the 2029/30 campaign.

‌



Despite that wait, Masters has suggested progress is being made on ending the 3pm blackout and allowing all Premier League and EFL matches to be made available to broadcast.

Asked if English football is leaning towards the end of the blackout, Masters told talkSPORT: "Yes, but it's not just us involved in the decision about Article 48. It's us, the EFL and the FA.

"We've got to take that decision at some point in the future about whether things are going to change. It's not a decision for now. It's a decision we've got to make before the next set of domestic processes that the EFL and the Premier League are going to do.

‌



View 2 Images Richard Masters (Image: Getty Images)

"I'd say in about 18 months' time we'll come back to that decision about whether Article 48 should remain or not."

Masters' comments come after the Premier League launched a new streaming service in Singapore.

‌



'Premier League +' is poised to broadcast all 380 matches live and provide 24/7 coverage, in what is believed to be a testing ground for potential future streaming in the United Kingdom.

Simon Jordan, the talkSPORT presenter, has long called for the Premier League to have its own 'Netflix of Football' subscription service.

Sports.title: Andrew Balding writes new ending to £1.5m summer blockbuster with unbeaten Item
Sports.content:
Andrew Balding writes new ending to £1.5m summer blockbuster with unbeaten Item

The Juddmonte International was billed as a straight match between Ombudsman and Constitution River but both were well beaten at York

View 4 Images Item (left) masters Almaqam with Constitution River and Ombudsman (obscured) at York (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

Andrew Balding rewrote the ending of this year’s summer blockbuster, the £1.5 million Juddmonte International at York on Wednesday.

The annual highlight of the Sky Bet Ebor Festival provided box office excitement, but the contest’s two lead performers were overshadowed by the supporting cast.

For weeks punters had salivated over the first meeting of defending champion and 5-6 favourite Ombudsman and Aidan O’Brien’s best three-year-old the unbeaten French 2,000 Guineas, French Derby and Eclipse Stakes-winning colt Constitution River, 7-4. The bookies could barely split the pair who were expected to duel for the spoils of a race which is annually voted best horse in the world.

Top jockey dies of injuries from heavy fall just weeks after winning nation’s biggest race READ MORE :

But while the Aidan O’Brien-trained Constitution River and Godolphin’s Ombudsman, plus their pacemakers, fought their own private battle, they were completely upstaged by two previously lesser lights.

While Ryan Moore chose to sit forward on Constitution River, William Buick was anchored at the back on Ombudsman.

Moore made the first move on Constitution River in the straight but he was unable to get clear of his rivals and while Ombudsman challenged along the far rail.

Yet they were soon overhauled first by Almaqam who kicked clear into what looked like a winning advantage only to be nailed near the line by Item, trained by Balding for sponsors Juddmonte. Constitution River was third with Ombudsman fourth.

View 4 Images Winning jockey Colin Keane with Item (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

It was a remarkable performance by the colt, winning for the third time at York, given he was nearly a doubt for the race.

“It was a 5am decision to get on the box to get here,” said Balding. “At the time of declaration he wasn’t running. They found a little blood blister in his foot but this morning he was a pain-free.

“Everything bar the last 48 hours had gone to plan and the way he jogged up this morning we were happy it wasn’t going to be an issue. It was an unorthodox preparation because usually our runners come up the night before and he had to leave at the crack of dawn.”

Balding is enjoying a golden summer, having claimed the King George VI and Queen Elizabeth Stakes with Kalpana in July.

View 4 Images Item (left) pounces on Almaqam (Image: Getty Images)

“It’s been amazing,” he went on. “We have been extremely lucky to be sent these horses in the first place. There are probably any number of trainers who would have done well with the horses they’ve been sent. It’s been a fantastic ride. Keep the money in-house. Those were my instructions from the Prince!”

Conditions had changed significantly to when the runners were declared a morning of rain on the Knavesmire.

O'Brien said: "The rain got into the ground a little bit but he ran very well. It was his first run back for a while.

View 4 Images Colin Keane with the trophy (Image: Richard Sellers/PA Wire)

"Ryan ended up maybe getting there a little bit earlier than he wanted then he got a little bit tired. Then he ended up getting beat!

"Maybe because he did a lot of things not right there could be a bit more to come. The horse that comes here always goes to Leopardstown for the Irish Champion Stakes."

John Gosden, co-trainer of Ombudsman said: "He just didn't like the ground. It's gone on the soft side and that's not his scene. He likes the faster, quicker ground. It played to others, not to him."

‌



He couldn’t have gone much closer under a penalty when beaten a shorthead on the all-weather at Southwell.

Given the tiny margin of defeat and the fact he found trouble before finishing strongly, it’s not hard to argue he was the best horse in the race. He should also improve for today’s step up to 7f for the first time. Have 1pt each-way at 12-1. A couple of bookies are paying six places.

OOLONG POOBONG (5.20) had little chance for a low draw in the Kensington Palace Stakes at Royal Ascot on just her second start of the season. She had looked a promising filly last year and, although she has been running well over a mile, her last victory came over today’s 7f distance.

It could well all come together in this handicap. Have 1pt each-way at 16-1. Sky Bet is offering six places.

Sports.title: Sheffield United could face massive points deduction after owners liquidated
Sports.content:
Sheffield United could face massive points deduction after owners liquidated

Championship side Sheffield United could potentially suffer a 12‑point deduction in the new season, after the company used to purchase the Yorkshire team was placed into liquidation by the High Court

View 2 Images Prince Abdullah bin Mosaad bin Abdulaziz Al Saud initiated legal action against Sheffield United's current owners

Sheffield United are facing the threat of a 12‑point deduction in the Championship after the company used to purchase the club was placed into liquidation by the High Court on Wednesday. Saudi Arabian Prince Abdullah Bin Mosaad Bin Abdulaziz Al Saud sold Sheffield United to Helmy Eltoukhy and Steven Rosen for just over £100million in December 2024.

‌



But Prince Abdullah's company, United World, is now seeking to wind up the takeover vehicle, COH Sports Bidco Ltd, claiming it still owes £35m in outstanding instalments from the sale. United World said in a statement that it had made 'every effort to resolve this matter amicably' but had 'received no response.'

‌



The petition was heard at the specialist Insolvency and Companies Court (ICC) in London on Wednesday (August 19) and lasted around 10 seconds. With no lawyers present on behalf of the club's new owners, COH Sports Bidco was formally placed into liquidation, and the Official Receiver will now take control of the company.

‌



Angus Groom, representing United World, requested the 'usual compulsory order,' which Judge Paul Greenwood granted, formally placing CSBL into liquidation. The company will now be wound up unless the £35m dispute is resolved.

A spokesperson on behalf of Sheffield United has claimed it does not impact the running of the club, however, saying: “Sheffield United Football Club is aware of today’s hearing at the High Court. This is a matter between the current owners and former owner. The Football Club is in contact with the EFL and the day-to-day operations at Sheffield United are unaffected.”

The EFL will assess the situation and determine whether it warrants a 12‑point deduction. "The EFL notes the High Court's decision to issue a winding up order on COH Sports Bidco Limited," they wrote in a statement.

‌



"The League will consider the implications of that development in line with its Regulations, including whether any further action is required. In addition, the EFL continues to consider other regulatory matters following changes to the Club's ownership structure and developments within the wider group.

"As these issues remain ongoing, the EFL will make no further comment at this stage."

Meanwhile, a statement from the Football Regulator (IFR) read: “We are examining the court's decision on COH Sport in detail, and we are in contact with the club and the EFL. The IFR can assess an incumbent owner's honesty, integrity and financial soundness under its Owners, Directors and Senior Executives regime, should it have grounds for concern. We are unable to comment further at this stage."

‌



View 2 Images Sheffield United have reacted to the latest news (Image: Maynard Manyowa/Getty Images)

The dispute centres around the decision to transfer Sheffield's shares from previous parent company CSBL to another one called 1919 Partners earlier this summer. Prince Abdullah claims that is an attempt to 'avoid paying CSBL's creditors.'

United World previously said in a statement: "If the winding-up petition is granted on 19 August, as we expect, EFL Regulation 2.1.16 provides that Rosen must be disqualified from being a controlling owner and director of SUFC. He will no longer be able to be chairman, or a director, he will no longer be able to exercise any control over the club and will have to sell a significant proportion of his controlling interest in the club.

‌



"In addition, we understand that, once investigations are completed, there is a real prospect that the EFL may have to impose a 12-point deduction on SUFC under EFL Regulation 12.3, in order to 'protect the integrity and continuity of the League Competition' and 'the reputation of The League.'"

Get YOUR Mirror Football Newsletter Get our comprehensive football coverage, with news, updates, opinions, analysis and everything that matters to you, straight to your inbox. To get it, it's a quick and easy one-two: 1. Head THIS WAY 2. Enter your email and hit Subscribe

United World have hired leading sports lawyer Nick De Marco and added: "As the former owners of SUFC, United World does not want to see SUFC facing months of uncertainty that will follow the winding-up order being granted on 19 August, but in the absence of Eltoukhy and Rosen, both billionaires, agreeing to pay what they owe, we have no alternative but to take all legal steps to protect our interests."

‌



Meanwhile, football finance expert Kieran Maguire has weighed in on the ongoing situation at Bramall Lane. He told BBC Sheffield: "If they are dismissive of it, then all they can do is quickly show the transfers of the money at the appropriate dates and United World don't have a case. But at the same time, why would you pursue somebody for money if you had been paid?

"There's one of two things that have happened there if the Sheffield United case, of the current owners is as strong as they claim it to be. Either, A, it's nonsense, or B, the numbers involved are inaccurate and therefore it's not £35million which I think is actually sort of, £25m plus interest or something like that.

"There's a dispute about the quantum involved or you know, they have made the payments and for some reason, United World is denying receipts. But looking at the people that United World have got acting for them, I think, is it Jones Day, who are one of the big-hitting lawyer firms. They're not doing it for, you know, the cost of a big issue per hour, are they? They're going to be serious lawyers at serious money levels."
